articles.title: Inside Health - A new era for type 1 diabetes treatment - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Plus, how much do people really change their habits for a free coffee?
articles.body: Insulin has been used to treat type 1 diabetes for more than a century but now there is a new treatment being rolled out on the NHS that can delay the onset of the disease for years. Alongside, screening is gathering pace, identifying those that could benefit. So, is this the beginning of a new era for type 1 diabetes treatment? Dima and his mum Elena explain what it was like to be told that he had tested positive for developing type 1 diabetes and what it was like taking part in the trial for this new drug, teplizumab. Parth Narendran, a Professor of Diabetes Medicine at the University of Birmingham, and Consultant Paediatric Endocrinologist Dr Renuka Dias at Birmingham Women's and Children's Hospital, reveal how these changes are transforming treatment. In July, the NHS announced plans to incentivise us to walk a marathon a month by offering vouchers and discounts. But with scant detail on how the plan will actually work, we ask Joan Costa-i-Font, Professor of Health Economics at London School of Economics, what makes schemes like this succeed or fail. Plus, why are horse fly bites so painful? Dr Erica McAlister, an entomologist at the Natural History Museum, explains how the flies break into our skin, while consultant dermatologist Dr Alexandra Banner describes what’s happening in our bodies. Presenter: James Gallagher Producer: Hannah Robins

articles.body:
An eye surgeon says that fewer people have been seeking treatment for eye damage than after the UK's last total solar eclipse in 1999.

Millions across the UK on Wednesday witnessed the most significant solar eclipse in 27 years - which saw more than 90% of the Sun covered by the Moon.

Speaking to the BBC, Mr Alexander Ionides from Moorfield Eye Hospital said hospitals were "inundated" with worried patients in 1999, but said it seemed warnings about looking directly at the sun with the naked eye were "getting through".

He added that symptoms of eye damage can include a spot in the centre of your vision, which may appear grey or yellow. Symptoms can develop within hours, but sometimes take days to develop.

articles.title: Weekly type 2 diabetes jab could replace daily injections
articles.summary: Hundreds of thousands of people with type 2 diabetes could get access to a new weekly insulin jab to replace daily injections.
articles.body:
Hundreds of thousands of people with type 2 diabetes could get access to a new weekly insulin jab to replace daily injections, reducing the number needed each year by 86%.

Patients still have to wait for the treatment to be approved by the medicines regulator before it is made available on the NHS.

The treatment, known as Onswik and made by Eli Lilly, is said to work as well as daily insulin jabs but only needs to be injected once a week.

The charity Diabetes UK says it will help people manage their condition better, especially those who have extra care needs and who require help to inject every day.

Around 4.7 million people in the UK were living with diabetes in 2024-25, of which roughly 90% had type 2.

The condition means the body can't make enough of a hormone called insulin, or the insulin it makes doesn't work properly - also known as insulin resistance.

Diabetes UK says that around 1 in 4 people with type 2 diabetes takes insulin.

Moving from daily injections to a weekly jab is most likely to benefit those who need help with their injections.

That might include frailer people and those with sight loss, limited hand movement and learning disabilities.

People who have difficulty following the steps involved in a daily injection or those who struggle to stick to their treatment regime are also likely to be helped by the new drug.

Douglas Twenefour, head of clinical at Diabetes UK, said: "For some, especially those with additional care needs, moving from daily insulin injections to a once-weekly option could help manage their diabetes more easily, improving their quality of life.

"It's essential that everyone who could benefit is supported by their healthcare team to make informed decisions, and that this treatment helps reduce inequities in diabetes care."

Helen Knight, director of medicines evaluation at Nice, said the new treatment could make a "real difference to the day-to-day lives of people with type 2 diabetes, especially those who rely on a carer, family member or healthcare professional to help them inject".

She added: "This recommendation is the result of rigorous, evidence-based decision making, striking a balance between the benefits to patients and the best use of limited NHS funding."

The initial approval for the new treatment has come from the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (Nice), which is the body responsible for deciding what medication and treatments should be available on the NHS.

But before type 2 diabetes patients can access the treatment via the NHS it needs to be licensed by another body, the medicines regulator, the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA).

Health officials say they are waiting on the MHRA's ruling on the treatment "to understand whether it could be rolled out on the NHS".

Nice guidance applies to the NHS in England, but the NHS in Wales also frequently follows its recommendations.

They aren't automatically followed in Northern Ireland where they are reviewed by the Department of Health, and in Scotland the process is managed by the Scottish Medicines Consortium.

articles.title: GLP-1 boom could reshape restaurant bars as diners cut back on alcohol
articles.summary: A new report reveals a growing interest in drink choices among restaurant customers. The report found that health is already influencing some Americans' decisions about alcohol.
articles.body: The rise of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs could be changing more than what Americans put on their plates, as restaurants increasingly look to wellness drinks and other alternatives to traditional alcoholic beverages. The National Restaurant Association's new 2026 Restaurant Beverage Trends report found growing interest in a wider range of drink choices, particularly among younger consumers, as restaurants experiment with everything from wellness and energy drinks to smoothies, lemonades and alcohol-free cocktails. Chad Moutray, chief economist at the Washington, D.C.-based National Restaurant Association, told Fox News Digital that the growing use of GLP-1 medications is one of several health trends restaurant operators are watching. MOVER OVER, APEROL: VIRAL ITALIAN SPRITZ ARRIVES IN US WITH EYE-CATCHING TWIST The report, which was conducted by the National Restaurant Association and is based on surveys of consumers and restaurant operators across the country, found that health is already influencing some Americans' decisions about alcohol. Among adults surveyed who said they don't drink alcohol, 25% cited health reasons. That figure climbed to 34% among Gen Z nondrinkers. Several trends are converging as younger consumers become more health-conscious and GLP-1 medications become more widely used, Moutray said. "I think you're seeing a lot younger folks who are, in general, wanting to be healthier. You have the Make America Healthy Again movement, which is also driving some of this trend," he said. PROTEIN COFFEE IS EXPLODING IN POPULARITY AMONG ADULTS WORRIED ABOUT MUSCLE LOSS "You have people drinking energy drinks and health drinks and all those things. And then you add to that the GLP-1 notion, where if you're taking one of those drugs and your appetite is more suppressed, you're not going to drink as much alcohol." Restaurants are already preparing to broaden their drink selections. Among limited-service restaurant operators, 24% said they planned to add new wellness drinks in 2026, while 26% planned to add energy drinks, 29% smoothies and 27% lemonades. Just under half, 46%, planned to add new coffee offerings. "I think as GLP-1s become less expensive as this year goes on and as we move into 2027, you're going to see restaurant operators continuing to look for alternatives that can be good menu options for consumers that might be taking those drugs," Moutray said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Derek Brown, a hospitality consultant and founder of Drink Company, said he's also seeing GLP-1s contribute to a broader shift toward moderation. "Yeah, there's no doubt that GLP-1s are having an effect on the way that people consume," Brown told Fox News Digital. "And it's part of a basket of things that's contributing to people moderating more often." The drugs can affect people's appetites for both food and drinks, Brown said, potentially leading some customers to consume less alcohol or choose nonalcoholic alternatives. "I think that's clearly part of this entire moderation trend that we're seeing that's just a part of it, but it's significant enough, so I think that's certainly a real thing," Brown said. "And I definitely think that bars and restaurants are starting to feel that." The changing beverage landscape, however, doesn't necessarily mean younger Americans are abandoning alcohol. Sixty percent of Gen Z adults and 68% of millennials said they drink alcohol at restaurants. Moutray believes younger consumers are instead choosing from a broader portfolio of drinks. The report found that 87% of full-service operators and 80% of limited-service operators said beverages can be an important driver of customer traffic. articles.title: Major brain changes that occur around age 50 could impact dementia risk
articles.summary: Microglia decline after age 50 as inflammatory blood-derived immune cells infiltrate the hippocampus, potentially driving neuroinflammation and dementia.
articles.body: The brain may undergo a notable shift at midlife, as new research suggests that its protective immune cells begin to decline and are increasingly replaced by inflammatory cells at around age 50. Researchers from the University of California, San Diego; New York Genome Center; and University of California, Irvine, found that these brain changes may help explain why aging increases the chances of neuroinflammation and neurodegenerative disease, including dementia. The study analyzed postmortem tissue from the hippocampus – the portion of the brain that is responsible for learning and memory – in 40 neurologically healthy adults, ranging from 20 to 95 years of age. THE 'AGE' OF YOUR BLOOD COULD PREDICT DEMENTIA RISK, NEW STUDY SUGGESTS "The most striking change was that after about age 50, the brain’s resident immune cells, called microglia, appear to be increasingly replaced by immune cells that enter from the bloodstream," first author Nathan Zemke, Ph.D., principal investigator at the UC San Diego Center for Epigenomics, told Fox News Digital. "Microglia normally protect the brain by clearing debris and responding to injury, but the incoming cells carry stronger inflammatory signals." The researchers believe this shift may contribute to chronic inflammation linked to cognitive decline and neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer’s. They also noted the deterioration of cells involved in maintaining the blood-brain barrier – the protective filter that helps keep harmful substances out of the brain – as well as widespread changes in DNA and gene activity. 'LONGEVITY GENE' MAY PROTECT THE BRAIN FROM ALZHEIMER'S BY BOOSTING DNA REPAIR, STUDY FINDS One of the most exciting implications of the study, according to Zemke, is that the replacement immune cells originate in the blood, which means they are more accessible than cells already deep inside the brain. "It may eventually be possible to modify blood-derived immune cells so that they are more protective and less inflammatory when in the brain," he said. "That could provide an entirely new way to approach Alzheimer’s and other neurological diseases without having to directly manipulate cells within the central nervous system." Although these findings are still in early stages, Zemke said, gaining a better understanding of why this immune-cell replacement happens – and why it happens earlier in some people than others – could lead to new strategies for preserving brain health during aging. The study’s chief limitation is that it studied human brain tissue collected postmortem from different individuals across the adult lifespan, the researchers noted. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "That allows us to identify strong age-related patterns, but it cannot directly show how the same person’s brain changes over decades or prove that a particular cellular change causes cognitive decline or Alzheimer’s disease," Zemke said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "We also do not yet know what triggers the influx of blood-derived immune cells into the brain. Determining whether changes in the blood-brain barrier, inflammation, genetics, lifestyle or other factors initiate this process will be an important next step." The researcher emphasized, however, that he would not recommend that people make any specific medical or lifestyle changes based on this study alone.  "These findings are primarily about understanding the biology of brain aging and identifying new directions for prevention and treatment," he said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES The timing and extent of the brain changes varied considerably between individuals, suggesting that brain aging is not necessarily a fixed process that happens identically in everyone. "The next challenge is to understand what drives that variation and whether some of those factors can be modified," Zemke added. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The study also included a small sample of just 40 people and examined tissue only from the hippocampus, meaning the findings may not reflect immune changes throughout the entire brain. The study, which was funded by the National Institutes of Health, was published in the journal Science.

articles.title: 1 in 4 NFL players who died from 2016 to 2021 had CTE, study finds
articles.summary: The study also found dementia was common among brain donors, with researchers urging prevention measures across all levels of the sport.
articles.body: At least 1 in 4 former NFL players who died from 2016 to 2021 was found to have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), according to a study released on Tuesday. Out of the 878 former players who died during that time frame, 235 donated their brains, researchers said, with 215 of those donated brains found to have CTE, a degenerative disease that can only definitively be diagnosed after death. An NFL spokesperson said: “The NFL continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts. “The NFL remains committed to ensuring that the NFL community has access to a robust — and expanding — set of resources to enhance their physical and mental well-being. “We encourage former players to utilize these resources to identify and seek treatment when they are concerned about their health.” The study’s lead author, Daniel Daneshvar, the chair of physical medicine and rehabilitation at Mass General Brigham and an associate professor at Harvard Medical School, said that repeated traumatic brain injuries are a known factor in elevated rates of neurodegenerative disease. “Similarly, we and others have shown that in NFL players, specifically, there is about a four times higher rate of death from neurodegenerative disease than the general population,” he added. The study from Mass General Brigham, Boston University and the Concussion & CTE Foundation also found dementia was common among brain donors, with researchers urging prevention measures that focus on cutting down on repetitive head impacts across all levels of the sport. “The bulk of the head impacts that these former NFL players experienced didn’t occur at the NFL level. They occurred at the collegiate level ... and at the high school level and in many cases the youth level. And all of those cumulative hits to the head added up to result in an increased risk,” said Daneshvar. The NFL’s 2011 Collective Bargaining Agreement limited the number of contact practices during the season. The Ivy League banned full-contact tackling during practices five years later. The Supreme Court cleared the way for the NFL’s settlement of concussion-related lawsuits with thousands of retired players in 2016. “If the changes that have been implemented at the NFL level, including reducing the amount of contact in sports practices to less than one per week, were propagated at the collegiate, high school and youth levels, athletes would be better off,” said Daneshvar, who urged current and former athletes experiencing cognitive symptoms to seek a neurodegenerative disease expert evaluation. “We know that nearly 70% of head impacts are occurring in practice. So without changing a single minute of game time at any of those levels, we can be substantially reducing the cumulative head impact burden that these individuals are experiencing throughout their lives.”

articles.title: Two unvaccinated people die of measles in Pennsylvania outbreak, health officials say
articles.summary: They are the first measles-related deaths in the U.S. this year.
articles.body: Two unvaccinated people have died of measles in Pennsylvania’s Lancaster County, the state’s health department confirmed Tuesday. Pennsylvania Secretary of Health Dr. Debra Bogen declined to give any additional information about the deaths during a media briefing, citing patient confidentiality. They are the first measles-related deaths in the U.S. this year and the first in Pennsylvania in 35 years. Lancaster County has seen the majority of measles cases in the state’s growing outbreak. As of Tuesday, 393 cases have been confirmed in the state; 86 of them were diagnosed in the past week. So far, 70 people have been hospitalized in Pennsylvania for measles complications. “These tragic deaths remind us that measles is not a harmless illness,” Dr. Jeffrey Martin, a physician at Penn Medicine Lancaster General Hospital, said during the briefing, which was held at Lancaster General Health’s Women & Babies Hospital. “It’s appropriate that we’re having this press conference at our Women & Babies Hospital. Pregnant women and children are vulnerable to measles if they are not vaccinated,” he said. Officials declined to answer a question about whether the deaths involved either a pregnant woman or a baby. Earlier this month, President Donald Trump signed an executive order meant to drive down the number of vaccines recommended for children. The move, which was backed by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., drew sharp criticism from pediatricians and public health experts. Kennedy has a history of anti-vaccine rhetoric and, according to local reporting in 2021, was a keynote speaker at an event in Lancaster County in which he said, without citing scientific evidence, that vaccines are harmful. During Tuesday’s media briefing, Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro said Kennedy had called him to offer resources to assist in the outbreak response. Shapiro said he declined the offer. “I was very, very blunt with him, and I made very clear that his actions and the rhetoric that’s coming from this administration are having a negative impact on communities across America, particularly right here in Pennsylvania,” Shapiro said. “There’s real-life consequences to scaring people and not relying on actual doctors and actual medical professionals to provide unbiased information to parents.” In a statement, HHS and the CDC expressed condolences to the families and communities affected by the measles deaths. “CDC is working closely with state and local health departments to strengthen response efforts, rapidly support affected communities across the state, and communicate the steps people can take to slow the spread of measles,” the statement said. The grim news comes at a time when more parents than ever are actively avoiding vaccines for their children. During the 2025-26 school year, 4.2% of kindergartners, about 155,000 kids, had at least one vaccine exemption, up from 3.6% the previous school year, according to recent data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The number of kids getting the MMR vaccine in Lancaster County, too, has been falling steadily, from 95.5% in 2017 to 87.6% in 2025. According to the CDC, 2,777 measles cases have been reported nationwide this year, the highest number in 35 years. As of Aug. 20, 193 people with measles, about 7% of cases, had been hospitalized this year. The majority of infected people are unvaccinated. More than 900 measles cases have been counted in the U.S. since May, with Pennsylvania accounting for more than a third of those new cases. Three people died of measles last year: an adult in New Mexico and two young girls in Texas. The measles, mumps and rubella vaccine, given in two doses around age 1 and age 5, offers 97% protection against measles, usually for life. Children as young as 6 months are eligible for an early, extra dose of the MMR vaccine during outbreaks. “When enough eligible individuals receive the vaccine, the entire community develops a level of immunity that protects our most vulnerable, including babies who are too young to be vaccinated,” Dr. Andrew Racine, president of the American Academy of Pediatrics, wrote in a statement. “I encourage all parents and caregivers to talk with your pediatrician and ask if your child is up-to-date on their MMR vaccine.”

articles.title: What Are Weight Loss Patches, and Do They Work?
articles.summary: Weight loss patches pop up online, but are they safe and do they work? Here’s what experts have to say.
articles.body:
"Hearst Magazines and Yahoo may earn commission or revenue on some items through these links."

It's tempting to start searching for extra help if you've tried to lose weight but haven't had much success. While GLP-1 medications are slowly becoming more affordable and accessible, their still-hefty price tag puts them out of reach for many. With that, you may be curious about whether weight loss patches could help you achieve your goals.

Meet the experts : Jessica Cording, R.D., is author of The Little Book of Game Changers ; Keri Gans, R.D., is author of The Small Change Diet ; Gina Keatley, C.D.N., is co-owner of Keatley Medical Nutrition Therapy ; Mir Ali, M.D ., is the medical director of MemorialCare Surgical Weight Loss Center at Orange Coast Medical Center in Fountain Valley, California; Ife J. Rodney, M.D ., is founding director of Eternal Dermatology + Aesthetics

These stickers come in a range of prices, but they're still a fraction of the cost of list-price GLP-1s and can be purchased without seeing a doctors, making them understandably appealing. They go by names like "GLP-1 patches," "fit patches," and "slimming patches," and are small enough to hide under your clothes.

But what are weight loss patches and, more importantly, do they work? Simply put, doctors are wary—for a bunch of reasons. Consider this your primer before adding weight loss patches to your cart.

Weight loss patches are bandages that contain certain ingredients the manufacturers claim will help the wearer lose weight. Once the adhesive patches are applied, they're supposed to transfer the ingredients to your body over time.

There are different weight loss patches on the market, including some that contain a little ball of ingredients that goes inside your belly button (and are held in place by the adhesive).

What do weight loss patches claim to do?

Each weight loss patch has slightly different claims, but the overarching idea is that they can help you lose weight. Some patches promise to " boost metabolism ," " curb cravings ," and " burn excess fat ." At least one claims to block fat absorption in the body.

While some patches say that they're backed by science, they don't actually show the research.

These patches are considered supplements and therefore aren't tightly regulated by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). As a result, it's hard to know for sure what is in them, points out Jessica Cording, R.D., author of The Little Book of Game Changers . However, the following ingredients come up often with weight loss patches:

Acai . Acai is a type of fruit that is "packed with antioxidants which may lead to decreased inflammation in the body," says Keri Gans, R.D., author of The Small Change Diet . "However, believing that leads to weight loss when absorbed through the skin is not scientifically proven at all," she adds.

Green coffee extract . This is "basically coffee beans that haven't been roasted," Cording says, adding that there's "not a lot of research on them and weight loss." Green coffee extract "has been associated with a decrease in fat cells and increase in energy" when it's eaten, Gans says. But, she adds, "it's not even conclusively proven" to help you lose weight when it's ingested and certainly not proven when it's applied to your skin.

Garcinia cambogia . Garcinia cambogia is believed to suppress appetite, but is not scientifically proven to work, Gans says. Cording calls this ingredient a "big red flag," noting that it's been associated with liver toxicity.

Berberine . This plant compound has been dubbed " nature's Ozempic ." While it's been linked with modest weight loss, it's unclear what kind of effect, if any, it would have in a patch form.

Ultimately, "weight loss patches can have any kind of variable substance in them," says Mir Ali, M.D ., medical director of MemorialCare Surgical Weight Loss Center at Orange Coast Medical Center in Fountain Valley, California. "I just haven't seen convincing evidence that any of these work," he adds.

It's difficult to say with certainty what the side effects can be from weight loss patches, given that it's hard to know what's actually in them, Cording says. However, experts say a few things could happen.

"With the patches, the body may not be able to absorb any benefit from these food products," says Gina Keatley, C.D.N., co-owner Keatley Medical Nutrition Therapy . "Our skin is not great at absorbing stuff—which is a good thing—but to increase absorption, some manufacturers may use chemicals that help bring 'stuff' through the skin and into the bloodstream." This, she says, is dangerous because your skin's protective barrier can't differentiate between good nutrients and things like harmful heavy metals.

Also, if you're on any medications, Gans says that there's a chance using a weight loss patch could interfere with your medication's effectiveness.

How do weight loss patches impact your skin?

This is a valid question, given that these patches literally stick onto your skin. The potential impact of these patches on your skin largely depends on what's in them, says Ife J. Rodney, M.D ., founding director of Eternal Dermatology + Aesthetics.

But sticking anything regularly to your skin can cause issues, she says. "The contact of those substances on your skin can cause contact dermatitis irritation," Dr. Rodney says. "It can also increase sweat and irritation in the area." What's more, the potential for irritation may be greater if you keep applying patches to the same spot.

Experts say there's really no data to support using these. Keatley strongly discourages people from using weight loss patches. "Ask yourself, why patches?" she says. "If your life is so hectic that the only way to get weight loss is a patch, then you may be very, very out of balance."

Instead, she suggests taking three days to track your meals. "See if you're eating too little or too much and start there," she says. "Skip the patches."

Cording also recommends taking a pass on using weight loss patches. "They are so ridiculous," she says. "These are not a reliable weight-loss option."

Because so little is known about weight loss patches and what's in them, it's difficult to say that they're safe. "Best case scenario is we don't have research to support that they work," Cording says. Worst case, depending on their ingredients, they may cause serious effects to your health.

Dr. Ali agrees. "We have no data to suggest that these are safe or that they work," he says.

Weight loss patches vs. GLP-1 medications

There is a big difference between weight loss patches and GLP-1 medications beyond price tag. GLP-1 medications like semaglutide and tirzepatide have been rigorously studied in clinical trials, suggesting that they're safe and effective to use for weight loss, Dr. Ali points out. "Weight loss patches have not been through any of that," he says.

GLP-1 medications also work through specific pathways in your body to tamp down cravings, lower feelings of hunger, and slow digestion, Dr. Ali explains. It's unclear if weight loss patches can achieve any of that, he says.

What to do if you're considering using weight loss patches

Experts universally agree that weight loss patches are not a good idea, and may even be dangerous for your health. If you're tempted to use weight loss patches, Dr. Ali recommends consulting with a healthcare professional first.

"Talk about what your goals are," he says. "If you have significant weight to lose, there are much better tools available—dietary counseling, medications, even surgery."

Dr. Ali says it's "not realistic" to expect big changes from sticking a patch on your skin. "It's really important to focus on changing your eating habits and eating the right things," he says. And, if that's not effective for you, it's time to rope in a professional for personalized guidance.

articles.title: Turmeric is good. That doesn’t mean you need supplements.
articles.summary: Psst — no supplement is going to stop you from aging.
articles.body:
Want more stories like this? Subscribe to our menopause newsletter .

A few months ago, I was at an event when a woman came up to me with a request for this newsletter: "Will you please write about turmeric?"

She had seen a flurry of content on Instagram about turmeric and its anti-inflammatory properties. On account after account, women were talking about how beneficial it was for midlife and the perimenopause transition especially. They weren't just talking about cooking with the yellow spice, commonly used in Middle Eastern and South Asian cooking; they were talking about supplements. So she bought a giant bottle and started taking them — and then when she mentioned this to her doctor at her next check-up, her doctor told her to stop immediately.

Turmeric can decrease the efficacy of tamoxifen, a drug used to prevent estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer — and one she was on.

It's a good reminder: There are many potions and pills touted online, promising "wellness." In reality? Lots of things that seem harmless at worst and good at best can actually hurt.

So for her and the rest of us, I called up some experts to learn more about the turmeric trend.

First I spoke to Dr. Nirupa Raghunathan , an internist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New York. She's also an integrative medicine specialist there, so no stranger to thinking about holistic habits to support health.

Raghunathan said as a person of South Asian heritage, she finds it fascinating to see the way a common ingredient for some cultures takes on superpower-like qualities in certain spaces.

"Turmeric is interesting because it is a spice like almost anything else," she said. "We can attribute qualities to spices partly based on flavor, partly on what we pass down in terms of what people believe."

Studies have shown that turmeric can have one notable anti-inflammatory benefit, specifically in regards to joint inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis.

Preclinical research — which doesn't involve looking at effects on a full living human body — has indicated some potential benefits for the immune system, brain health and digestion. And some studies looking at large populations show that diets rich in turmeric are linked to longer lifespans. Research like this gives turmeric the sheen of being a "health food."

What happens next, Raghunathan said, is that people assume that a turmeric supplement is a natural version of ibuprofen. Except this isn't really true at all.

There are two big differences between cooking with turmeric and taking it as a supplement: concentration and interval.

The active component in turmeric, the one linked to anti-inflammatory effects, is the chemical curcumin. In supplements, you can't tell from a label what level of curcumin concentration there is. Some also have piperine, or black pepper oil, added to make the curcumin more absorbable and thus more potent. (It might be listed on the label as either piperine or black pepper oil; sometimes it's listed as part of a "proprietary blend.")

On top of that, when you consume a spice you cook with, you're eating smaller amounts of it stretched over the length of time it takes to eat a full meal, whereas a supplement gives a much higher amount of the active chemicals in a quick burst.

That's why Diane McKay, PhD , program director and assistant professor at the Friedman School of Nutrition Science and Policy at Tufts University and an expert on the role that nutrients and bioactive compounds play in healthy aging, reminds us that we already have a great way to get nutrients without buying a single bottle of pills.

"We recommend food first," McKay said. "Try to get all of your nutrients as well as your phytonutrients and all of these other bioactive types of compounds that you find in plant-based foods and try to get them from food first because they're present with other nutrients and other compounds in the food that often optimize their intake and utilization by the body. When you isolate something and put it into a supplement, it may have a different effect."

Raghunathan said that when she speaks to patients about turmeric, she always begins by explaining that turmeric is great to use in food.

"Have a turmeric latte if you want! Throw it into a smoothie in a reasonable dose!"

But supplements, she said, are a whole other story.

Curcumin is known to interact with certain liver enzymes, which means taking turmeric supplements can impact how you absorb any medication. And the piperine can have its own drug interactions.

"If you're on multiple, complex medications, you should avoid it," Raghunathan said of turmeric supplements.

(Great time to offer a general reminder that you should always talk to your doctor before beginning to take any kind of over-the-counter supplement!)

Buyer beware (you're still going to age)

It's also important to remember that no supplement is going to "fix" the natural process of aging.

Supplement manufacturers do not have to follow the same regulatory standards as pharmaceutical companies overseen by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). Some may have pesticides and contaminants, and many are not transparent about their sourcing.

McKay advises extra caution when it comes to buying supplements you see marketed and sold by influencers online.

Increasingly, she said, she hears midlife influencers talking about turmeric supplements as some kind of miracle pill, a magical way to eliminate inflammation and promote longevity. This conversation is divorced from the role the actual spice holds in the culinary traditions of many cultures and also is rarely backed by any kind of substantive research.

"It's not a general panacea," McKay said. "Healthy aging doesn't come from one of these single, hero ingredients. It comes from patterns: what we eat every day, how we move, our sleep patterns, the social connections we make."

Raghunathan points out that Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center even has its own online " About Herbs " checker, where you can research supplements to find out any potential interactions they may cause.

"I think it's nice to think that something from nature is invariably going to be the best thing for us." But reality is more complicated than that, Raghunathan said — something she knows even as an integrative medicine specialist herself.

"When I have a headache, I still take an Advil. I don't go to curcumin," she said.

Concerned about inflammation? Moderate your intake of foods that are known to increase inflammation in the body — like added sugars, added saturated fat and added sodium.

And use turmeric when it makes sense, Raghunathan said.

"I strongly suggest if you want to include turmeric in your food, go to the spaces where culturally they've been doing it for a long time because it usually tastes better. Lentils with turmeric? It's been done in India for thousands of years, so it tastes better, probably, than trying to add turmeric in your mac and cheese."

articles.title: Muere Dolly Parton, la reina del country, a los 80 años
articles.summary: Su sobrino ha anunciado la noticia en un comunicado que ha dado pie a cientos de mensajes de compañeros y admiradores
articles.body:
La música no volverá a ser nunca igual sin Dolly Parton, icono intergeneracional que ha puesto la banda sonora a miles de historias. La voz de la reina del country se ha apagado para siempre a los 80 años tras una enfermedad que nunca le quitó las ganas de seguir adelante. Su problema de salud tampoco minimizó su entrega absoluta por una profesión que se ha quedado huérfana con su inesperada muerte. Ha sido su sobrino quien ha confirmado la triste noticia en un comunicado que ha causado una gran conmoción ya que hace solo unos días la propia cantante se pronunció públicamente acerca de su estado y sus planes de futuro.

"Mi nombre es Brin Seaver, hijo de Cassie Parton, y hoy represento a las familias Parton y Owens para anunciar el fallecimiento de mi tía, Dolly Rebecca Parton Dean, hermana, sobrina y abuela de una generación y Gigi de la siguiente. Este anuncio en video es algo que Dolly me pidió hace años, antes de que lo asimilara por completo como una realidad futura. Como su jefe de seguridad durante más de dos décadas, un cargo que mi padre, Larry, desempeñó antes que yo, había imaginado la gravedad de este momento, pero no la había sentido realmente hasta ahora", ha dicho en un anuncio cuya repercusión ha sido máxima en escasos segundos. Se ha desatado una oleda de mensajes de compañeros que se quedan huérfanos sin ella.

Los detalles de su funeral y el testimonio de su círculo íntimo

La familia de Dolly Parton ha avanzado cómo va a ser la despedida de la artista. Siguiendo sus propios deseos, harán "un pequeño servicio fúnebre privado para los más cercanos" . Animan a todos los admiradores y amigos de la intérprete de 9 to 5 a rendirle homenaje en las redes sociales etiquetando su cuenta o dejando un mensaje en su web oficial. Además, piden que no se compren flores para ella y que ese dinero lo donen a la Imagination Library, iniciativa creada por la propia cantante para fomentar la lectura.

También le han dedicado unas emotivas palabras en las que la definen como una mujer "con una vida llena de brillo que resplandeció con tanta intensidad que todo el mundo pudo verla". "Dolly seguirá siendo para siempre una fuente de inspiración, no solo por su música atemporal y su prolífica carrera como compositora, sino también por su ingenio, calidez y amabilidad, que nos hacían sentir a todos como una familia. El legado de Dolly Parton es de amor, compasión y resiliencia", han añadido. También han remarcado que durante las siete décadas en las que se extendió su carrera "inspiró a múltiples generaciones de artistas y seguidores con su música y su compromiso inquebrantable por hacer del mundo un lugar mejor". Sus canciones, sostienen, seguirán resonando en personas de todas las edades, y su labor filantrópica tendrá un impacto duradero.

La última aparición de Dolly Parton cuatro días antes de su muerte

En medio de la preocupación por la cancelación de los conciertos que tenía previstos para diciembre, la ganadora de 10 premios Grammy tomaba la palabra para hablar en primera persona de su situación. Fue el pasado 21 de agosto cuando se dirigió a sus fans, repartidos por todos los rincones del planeta, para contarles mediante People que estaba lidiando con algunos problemas de salud a los que no les prestó atención cuando cuidaba de su marido. Recordaba que no era la primera vez que se enfrentaba a una situación así porque a principios de los 80 tuvo problemas ginecológicos y de peso.

A pesar de haber atravesado otros episodios complejos, quiso dar su propia versión de los hechos consciente de que ahora la realidad que nos rodea es otra ya que todo es magnifica por el impacto de las redes sociales. "Solía bromear diciendo que era la reina de los tabloides, ¡pero ahora supongo que puedo decir que soy la reina de la IA en las redes sociales! Hablando en serio, aunque todavía me estoy recuperando, ¡sigo trabajando! Ya me conocen, como he dicho muchas veces, me he obsesionado con mis sueños y aún tengo muchas cosas que quiero lograr, así que voy a seguir trabajando todo el tiempo que pueda para verlas hacerse realidad" , aseguraba.

El gran mazazo que la cantante no pudo superar

La vida de Dolly Parton se paró para siempre en marzo de 2025 con la muerte de su gran amor . Carl Thomas Dean fue su compañero incondicional durante 60 años en los que siempre se mantuvo en un segundo plano. No la acompañó a actos públicos porque se sentía cómodo en la sombra, una posición desde la que aportaba calma, serenidad, un apoyo firme y normalidad a su mujer. Ella era una estrella internacional gracias a su talento y su voz, pero en ese brillo que desprendía también tenía un papel fundamental su marido, al que conoció de manera fortuita al salir de una lavandería.

Carl fue además un fuente de inspiración para la artista y así se refleja en canciones como Jolene , una de las más emblemáticas de su extensa discografía. Dolly, que renovó en 2016 los votos matrimoniales con su esposo, siempre compartió con naturalidad el secreto de su unión inquebrantable. "Siempre bromeo y me río cuando la gente me pregunta eso. Nuestra vida es sencilla, pero fácil. Ni siquiera nos hacemos tanta compañía. Viajo mucho, pero realmente disfrutamos el uno del otro cuando estamos juntos y de las pequeñas cosas ". Entre los planes sencillos de los que disfrutaban, viajes en su autocaravana o picnics cerca de casa.

La historia de Dolly Parton, una estrella hecha a sí misma

Ha batido récords en la música vendiendo 160 millones de discos, una cifra aún más increíble si se tiene en cuenta su historia. Dolly Parton nació en 1946 en Pittman Center, Tennessee, en el seno de una familia humilde y muy numerosa, rodeada por once hermanos. Tenía solo seis años cuando se adentró en la música mediante la iglesia, donde cantaba y tocaba la guitarra sin imaginar todo lo que estaba por venir. En 1964 se mudó a Nashville, donde se ganaba la vida tocando en locales. Fue así como llegó su primera gran oportunidad al ser contratada por Porter Wagoner para formar juntos dueto en el programa de televisión The Porter Wagoner Show.

En los 70, cuando ya había definido su característico look con melena rubia y ropa sensual, despegó como un fenómeno internacional al colocarse en el primer puesto de las listas country. Además, fue en esa década cuando compuso la canción que lo cambió todo: I Will Always Love You , un tema que popularizó Whitney Houston en El guardaespalda s, película que protagonizó con Kevin Costner . Y aquello a la vez le abrió las puertas del séptimo arte, en el que ha trabajado como actriz y cantante. Incluso ha ganado un Oscar honorífico y un Emmy, además de ser incluida en el Salón de la Fama de la música country.

Su parte más desconocida, junto a su trayectoria musical, quedaron plasmadas en Dolly Parton, Songteller: My Life in Lyrics. Además, su vida se llevó a las tablas con el montaje Dolly: A True Original Musical, que se estrenó el pasado verano y se estaba moviendo para llevarlo a Broadway a lo largo de este año 2026 . Porque la artista era mucho más que una voz. Destacaba también por su solidaridad, su apoyo a diferentes causas filantrópicas y su ayuda a compañeras más jóvenes como Miley Cyrus, a la que amadrinó profesionalmente. Hoy todas lloran su irreparable pérdida y escuchan en bucle su voz eterna.

articles.title: Deadly measles outbreak hits Northeast as state records first deaths in 35 years
articles.summary: Two unvaccinated Lancaster County residents died from measles, marking Pennsylvania's first measles deaths in 35 years amid 393 confirmed cases.
articles.body: Pennsylvania confirmed two measles-related deaths on Tuesday, according to the state’s department of health. This marks the first losses related to the highly contagious virus within the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania in 35 years. The Pennsylvania Department of Health (DOH) confirmed that both Lancaster County individuals were unvaccinated, noting that the best way to prevent measles infection is to get the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine. MEASLES SURGE HITS NEW MILESTONE AS US CASES SURPASS LAST YEAR'S TOTAL The MMR vaccine administered over two doses can boost a person’s immune system and provide 97% lifetime protection, according to health officials. In a press release, Pennsylvania Secretary of Health Dr. Debra Bogen shared her "deepest sympathies" with the "loved ones who are facing this unimaginable loss." "Because measles was largely eliminated in the Commonwealth for more than three decades, people are not familiar with this disease and don’t fully understand the potential severity of the illness," she said in the statement. "We want to ensure that every Pennsylvanian has the information they need to protect themselves, their loved ones and their communities." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "As a physician, I want to make sure that people understand the MMR vaccine is safe and provides the best protection we have against measles." The state's DOH has confirmed 393 cases of measles in 28 counties so far in 2026. Measles is a highly contagious virus that can be fatal in one to three patients per 1,000 cases, data shows. The virus can cause long-term health problems, including pneumonia and brain swelling. Nearly 20% of individuals who contract measles are hospitalized. Measles spreads when an infected person breathes, coughs or sneezes, spreading the virus through respiratory droplets. It can remain infectious in the air and on surfaces for up to two hours after the person leaves the area, experts caution. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Early measles symptoms include fever, cough, runny nose and red, watery eyes. A measles rash follows a few days later, starting on the head and spreading down to the rest of the body. Symptoms can start seven to 21 days after exposure. Those who believe they were exposed to measles should contact a healthcare provider. Dr. Jesse Goodman, former FDA chief scientist in Washington, D.C., spoke with Fox News Digital about the MMR vaccine, calling it "extremely safe and highly effective." "The vaccine prevents millions of measles deaths worldwide annually, including hundreds that used to occur in the U.S.," he said. "There is no evidence that MMR vaccine causes any chronic illnesses, including autism." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Dr. Amesh Adalja, senior scholar at the Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security in Baltimore, Maryland, agreed that Pennsylvania's 35-year streak without a measles-related death "wasn't luck." "It was the vaccine working so completely that an entire generation of parents grew up never seeing what this virus does to a child’s lungs or brain," he told Fox News Digital. "That protection is increasingly not valued, and this is the predictable result when the population turns their back on a life-saving technology." Dr. Marc Siegel, Fox News senior medical analyst, previously emphasized the highly contagious nature of measles amid elevated case counts across the U.S. "Measles is so contagious that up to 90% of susceptible people who are exposed to an infected person will become infected," he told Fox News Digital, stressing the importance of community protection. "We need a 95% vaccine coverage rate to ensure herd immunity," he said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The herd immunity threshold is a mathematical estimate based on how contagious a disease is and how effectively immunity from vaccination or prior infection prevents its spread, according to Siegel. "In this case, two-dose vaccination is almost 100% effective, and natural immunity after a measles infection is generally lifelong," the doctor said. "This isn’t about personal choice, it’s about community protection. We need to protect those who can’t have a live virus vaccine because they are immunocompromised or pregnant."

articles.title: Seven killed in Gaza as Israeli strike ‘destroys’ aid supply warehouse
articles.summary: Health Ministry warns of ‘complete collapse of the basic necessities of life’ in Gaza as Israel’s attacks continue.
articles.body:
Israeli strikes have killed at least seven Palestinians across Gaza, according to local medical sources, in ongoing violations of a “ceasefire” that went into effect last October.

Three Palestinians were killed and others injured in a strike on a home in Beit Lahiya, near Kamal Adwan Hospital, on Tuesday, a source at al-Shifa Hospital said.

Earlier in the day, a drone strike that hit a gathering of civilians killed a man in Khan Younis’s al-Mawasi area, and injured three others.

Three other Palestinians died from wounds they sustained in earlier Israeli raids on Khan Younis, said Al Jazeera Arabic correspondent Nour Khaled.

Two of them died from injuries suffered in an attack on Monday, while the third had been wounded about two weeks ago, she said.

An Israeli military strike overnight into Tuesday also destroyed a warehouse storing nutrition supplies intended for children, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers in Gaza, Medical Aid for Palestinians (MAP) said.

“The force of the explosion caused large sections of the building to collapse, including the roof and walls, completely burying supplies beneath the rubble,” MAP said in a statement.

“Humanitarian workers, humanitarian facilities and the supplies that people depend on must be protected,” it added.

The warehouse belongs to Ard El Insan (AEI), a local humanitarian organisation working with MAP to support about 60 medical points serving up to 100 women and children daily.

The overnight explosion collapsed large sections of the building, including the roof and walls, burying the supplies under rubble, according to MAP, which said the entire stock was damaged and rendered unfit for human consumption.

“Losing these quantities in their entirety is a major blow to our work and will undoubtedly affect our ability to reach the children and women who need these services, particularly given the conditions they continue to face in the aftermath of starvation,” said Sahar Salem, AEI’s project coordinator.

“Even with the ceasefire, conditions on the ground remain extremely challenging, and children and women still urgently need continued support, she added.

She said two of her colleagues have been killed and another wounded since Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza began.

Also on Tuesday, the head of Gaza’s Ministry of Health warned of “complete collapse of the basic necessities of life” amid critical oxygen supply shortages.

Speaking to Al Jazeera, Director-General Dr Munir al-Bursh said that Israel “continues to escalate its attacks on Gaza and violate the ceasefire agreement, which is present in statements but absent from people’s lives on the ground”.

Al-Bursh added that “only 12 oxygen stations remain operational out of around 34”, and warned that “any additional breakdown could cut off oxygen to patients”.

“If this oxygen supply stops, these people will die,” he said. “We do not want to reach the point where a doctor is forced to choose between two patients, deciding who receives oxygen and who is left without it.”

Ongoing Israeli attacks and ceasefire violations come despite US President Donald Trump’s call for Israel to halt its attacks.

In an interview with Fox News on August 17, Trump said that Israel “should not be striking in Gaza”, and that “Hamas agreed to lay down their weapons” under the terms of a US-backed peace plan.

articles.title: Homem morre em acidente entre caminhonete e carreta na BR-304 | G1
articles.standfirst: Ryan Carneiro dos Santos ficou preso às ferragens e morreu no local; motorista da carreta teve ferimentos leves e foi levado ao hospital.
articles.summary: Ryan Carneiro dos Santos morreu após uma colisão frontal entre uma caminhonete e uma carreta na BR-304, em Angicos, nesta quarta-feira (26).
articles.body:
Homem morre em acidente entre caminhonete e carreta na BR-304 — Foto: Letícia Jácome

Um homem morreu e outro ficou ferido em um acidente envolvendo uma caminhonete e uma carreta na BR-304, em Angicos, na região Central do Rio Grande do Norte. A colisão aconteceu por volta das 11h45 desta quarta-feira (26), no km 143 da rodovia.

Segundo a Polícia Rodoviária Federal (PRF), houve uma colisão frontal entre os dois veículos. A caminhonete era uma Volkswagen Saveiro, enquanto a carreta era formada por um cavalo-trator e um semirreboque.

O motorista da caminhonete foi identificado como Ryan Carneiro dos Santos. Ele ficou preso às ferragens e morreu ainda no local. O veículo ficou destruído com o impacto da batida.

O motorista da carreta teve ferimentos leves e foi socorrido para o Hospital Regional de Angicos.

Equipes da Polícia Militar e da Polícia Rodoviária Federal estiveram no local para atender a ocorrência. A Polícia Civil e a Polícia Científica também foram acionadas. A perícia foi realizada para auxiliar na apuração das circunstâncias do acidente.

O corpo de Ryan Carneiro dos Santos foi retirado do local e encaminhado ao Instituto Médico Legal (IML).

Durante o atendimento da ocorrência e a realização da perícia, o trânsito ficou interditado por mais de uma hora, segundo a PRF.

O Corpo de Bombeiros de Assú também foi acionado para realizar a limpeza da pista e auxiliar na segurança do trecho.

As circunstâncias da colisão e o que provocou a batida ainda serão investigados.

articles.title: Mamografia em João Pessoa: Léo Bezerra sanciona lei com vetos | G1
articles.standfirst: Texto aprovado por Léo Bezerra exige exame anual para prevenir câncer de mama. No entanto, artigos que obrigavam o município a garantir e agendar o procedimento foram vetados.
articles.summary: Mamografia em João Pessoa é obrigatória aos 40 anos após sanção de Léo Bezerra, mas vetos retiram dever do município de garantir e agendar os exames.
articles.body:
Mamografia de paciente com tumor pequeno na mama Hospital de Amor Barretos — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

O prefeito de João Pessoa , Léo Bezerra (PSDB), sancionou uma lei que torna obrigatória a realização do exame anual de mamografia em mulheres a partir dos 40 anos, em João Pessoa. A lei foi publicada no Diário Oficial do Município, nesta quarta-feira (26).

A lei é de autoria do vereador Marcos Vinícius (PDT) e foi aprovada com vetos. A proposta de lei tem como objetivo ampliar a prevenção e o diagnóstico precoce do câncer de mama.

A idade de 40 anos é considerada um marco pelas principais entidades médicas, como a Sociedade Brasileira de Mastologia (SBM), que recomenda o início do rastreamento mamográfico anual nessa faixa etária para mulheres de risco habitual.

O prefeito vetou os artigos 1º e 2º, que, segundo o texto original do projeto de lei, instituíam a obrigatoriedade da realização dos exames na saúde pública do município. Também foi vetado o artigo 5º, que obrigava os serviços públicos de saúde a garantir o agendamento e a realização do exame de mamografia para todas as mulheres elegíveis segundo a lei.

articles.title: Criança de 10 anos morre após ser atropelada no Itaim Paulista, Zona Leste de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima foi socorrida pelo Samu e levada a hospital, mas não resistiu aos ferimentos; motorista de 22 anos fez teste do bafômetro, que deu negativo.
articles.summary: Vítima foi socorrida pelo Samu e levada a hospital, mas não resistiu aos ferimentos; motorista de 22 anos fez teste do bafômetro, que deu negativo.
articles.body:
Pietro Tretin foi atropelado por motorista de 22 anos no Itaim Paulista, Zona Leste de SP. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

A Polícia Civil investiga o atropelamento que resultou na morte de uma criança de 10 anos na noite desta segunda-feira (24), na Rua Santa Rosa de Lima, barirro do Itaim Paulista, na Zona Leste de São Paulo .

A vítima foi identificada como Pietro Tretin Silva Caldeira. O velório está marcado para a manhã desta quarta-feira (26), no Cemitério Jardim Parque das Palmeiras, até as 11h. Em seguida, será realizado o sepultamento.

Policiais militares foram acionados e constataram que a criança havia sido atropelada por um motorista de 22 anos.

A vítima foi socorrida pelo Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) e levada ao Hospital Municipal Professor Doutor Alípio Corrêa Netto, mas não resistiu aos ferimentos.

Segundo a Secretaria da Segurança Pública (SSP), o motorista realizou teste do bafômetro, que apresentou resultado negativo para consumo de álcool.

A perícia foi acionada. O caso foi registrado no 63º Distrito Policial (Vila Jacuí) como atropelamento e homicídio culposo na direção de veículo automotor.

As circunstâncias do atropelamento são investigadas. Diligências estão em andamento para esclarecer o caso.

articles.title: Por que estudar na Unoeste? Conheça os diferenciais da universidade  | G1
articles.standfirst: Com ensino reconhecido pelo MEC, estrutura moderna e mais de 40 cenários de prática, instituição oferece formação conectada à realidade profissional
articles.summary: Com ensino reconhecido pelo MEC, estrutura moderna e mais de 40 cenários de prática, instituição oferece formação conectada à realidade profissional
articles.body:
Unoeste reúne laboratórios, ambientes de aprendizagem e diferentes cenários de prática para a formação dos alunos — Foto: Marcel Sabatino

Escolher onde estudar é uma decisão que pode influenciar não apenas os próximos anos, mas também os caminhos que serão percorridos ao longo da carreira.

Se você está em dúvida sobre qual universidade escolher para trilhar o seu futuro, conhecer por que estudar na Unoeste (Universidade do Oeste Paulista) pode ser o passo decisivo para transformar sua trajetória acadêmica e profissional.

Reconhecida como a melhor universidade particular do Estado de São Paulo, segundo avaliação máxima (nota 5) do Ministério da Educação (MEC), a Unoeste também figura entre as três melhores instituições privadas do Brasil.

Mas afinal, o que faz a Unoeste ser referência e por que vale a pena estudar ali?

Uma das características da formação oferecida pela Unoeste é a valorização das experiências práticas ao longo da graduação . A proposta é permitir que o estudante desenvolva conhecimentos técnicos e, ao mesmo tempo, competências importantes para atuar profissionalmente.

Na área da saúde, por exemplo, os alunos contam com mais de 40 cenários de prática por meio da rede de parcerias da instituição. A estrutura permite experiências em diferentes níveis de atenção e serviços, incluindo Atenção Primária, Secundária e Terciária em Saúde, SAMU, prontos atendimentos, prontos-socorros, instituições de assistência social e Clínica-Escola .

Também fazem parte dessa rede instituições como a Santa Casa de Jaú e o Hospital Amaral Carvalho, referência nacional no tratamento oncológico.

Para quem está se preparando para escolher uma profissão que exige contato direto com pessoas, essa vivência pode fazer diferença na formação.

Foi o que aconteceu com Natalia Martins Faria , formada em Medicina pela Unoeste em 2024 e atualmente residente de Clínica Médica no Hospital Estadual de Bauru. Para ela, o contato com a realidade profissional começou ainda nos primeiros momentos da graduação.

“Na minha graduação de Medicina na Unoeste tive a oportunidade de aprender com profissionais excelentes da área, além de ter contato com os pacientes desde o primeiro semestre do curso”, comenta.

Segundo Natalia, a experiência contribuiu para uma formação que combinou conhecimento técnico e atenção às necessidades dos pacientes .

“A Unoeste possibilitou uma formação humanizada e um cuidado integral à saúde do paciente. Além disso, forneceu uma base sólida de conhecimento teórico para o desenvolvimento das habilidades práticas”, finaliza.

Infraestrutura que faz parte da formação

Outro destaque que pesa na escolha de uma universidade é a infraestrutura disponível para os estudantes. Na Unoeste , o campus conta com 33 laboratórios equipados com tecnologia de ponta , além de ambientes pensados para diferentes metodologias de aprendizagem.

Entre os espaços está o Laboratório de Habilidades e Simulação , que possui 14 estações destinadas a treinamentos práticos e ao desenvolvimento de competências clínicas .

Suzana Cardoso Malagutti, estudante de Biomedicina, escolheu a Unoeste pela estrutura e destaca a experiência durante a graduação — Foto: Gabriel Ferracini

Para Suzana Cardoso Malagutti , estudante do 5º termo de Biomedicina , a estrutura foi um dos principais motivos para escolher a instituição.

“Escolhi a Unoeste não apenas pela proximidade com a minha cidade, mas principalmente pela estrutura excepcional que a faculdade oferece. Desde o primeiro dia, me senti acolhida em um ambiente preparado para nos proporcionar uma formação de qualidade”, relembra.

A estudante destaca especialmente os laboratórios e os materiais utilizados nas atividades acadêmicas.

“Os laboratórios são modernos e bem equipados, as salas de aula oferecem conforto e tecnologia, e há uma grande variedade de materiais disponíveis para complementar nossos estudos — o que é essencial para quem faz um curso tão prático e exigente como a Biomedicina”, finaliza.

O acompanhamento de professores e coordenadores também aparece entre os diferenciais destacados pelos estudantes.

Segundo a estudante Katley Karen Giroti Celestino , do 9º termo de Fisioterapia , ao pesquisar sobre a instituição antes de ingressar, ouviu boas referências sobre o ensino e encontrou na Unoeste uma experiência que correspondeu às expectativas.

“Os professores sempre são muito dispostos a tirarem nossas dúvidas e a coordenação do curso ouve cada opinião nossa e sempre procuram fazer o melhor para todos”, comenta.

Para Katley, a possibilidade de perguntar e retomar o conteúdo sem receio também contribui para o aprendizado.

“Tenho convicção em falar que nunca precisei ficar na dúvida de alguma matéria pelo receio de perguntar quantas vezes fosse necessário. A dinâmica das aulas é bem completa e não faltam os materiais necessários para cada uma delas”, afirma.

Os eventos acadêmicos também são apontados por ela como uma forma de complementar a aprendizagem e proporcionar novas experiências ao longo da graduação.

O futuro profissional começa na graduação

A escolha de uma universidade também está relacionada ao futuro profissional e ao mercado de trabalho (link: Para João Pedro Desiderá , estudante do 3º termo de Enfermagem , ingressar no ensino superior significa pensar no profissional que deseja se tornar.

Para João Pedro Desiderá, o contato diário com professores inspiradores torna mais concreta a experiência de construir a carreira durante a graduação — Foto: Gabriel Ferracini

“Quando estamos pensando em qual universidade devemos escolher para estudar, estamos traçando uma linha muito marcante sobre o que queremos para nós no futuro e tudo aquilo que queremos viver no caminho até lá”, fala.

O estudante afirma que sempre buscou uma instituição que pudesse ampliar suas possibilidades e contribuir para sua formação . Para ele, o contato cotidiano com os docentes ajuda a transformar esse objetivo em uma experiência concreta.

As experiências dos estudantes mostram que responder à pergunta “ por que estudar na Unoeste? ” envolve uma combinação de fatores: qualidade reconhecida, estrutura, professores, oportunidades práticas e um ambiente pensado para acompanhar a trajetória acadêmica .

Com mais de quatro décadas de atuação no ensino superior, mais de 120 mil profissionais formados e uma comunidade de aproximadamente 16 mil alunos e colaboradores, a instituição reúne diferentes possibilidades para quem deseja iniciar uma graduação, continuar os estudos ou investir na especialização profissional .

Seja para quem está saindo do ensino médio, buscando uma segunda graduação ou procurando uma formação que acompanhe as transformações do mercado, a escolha da universidade é uma etapa importante desse caminho.

articles.title: Jovem que morreu em madeireira trabalhava sem registro há 2 meses | G1
articles.standfirst: Proprietário da empresa afirmou que a vítima estava no primeiro dia de trabalho, mas ex-companheira diz que o jovem atuava no local havia pelo menos dois meses sem carteira assinada; caso é investigado pela Polícia Civil.
articles.summary: Proprietário da empresa afirmou que a vítima estava no primeiro dia de trabalho, mas ex-companheira diz que o jovem atuava no local havia pelo menos 2 meses sem carteira assinada.
articles.body:
A morte de Cauã Godoy, de 23 anos, após ser atingido por placas de madeira em uma marcenaria no Jardim São Gabriel, em Campinas , ganhou um fato novo nesta quarta-feira (26). Depois de o proprietário da empresa dizer que o funcionário estava no primeiro dia de trabalho, a ex-companheira de Cauã afirmou que ele atuava no local havia pelo menos dois meses sem registro em carteira .

"Não era o primeiro dia, porque ele era informal, né? Ele ia quando ele queria, aí nessa época que a gente terminou, ele deu uma parada de ir, estava na vida dele, e aí, quando ele retornou, foi na terça-feira", contou a jovem.

Após a manifestação da família, o proprietário da marcenaria foi procurado para esclarecer as informações sobre o vínculo de trabalho. O empresário não atendeu as ligações e, por mensagem, informou que enviaria uma nota, mas não voltou a responder até a publicação desta reportagem.

Em uma das mensagens, no entanto, o empresário disse que Cauã teria começado a trabalhar no início de agosto. O caso é investigado pela Polícia Civil.

Bruna Godoy ao lado do filho, Cauã, morto após ser atingido por placas de madeira no trabalho — Foto: Redes sociais

Segundo o advogado trabalhista Marcelo Mascaro, será preciso apurar se Cauã estava em seu primeiro dia de trabalho ou se já atuava informalmente na empresa.

Segundo ele, a investigação também deve analisar se a empresa adotava medidas de segurança obrigatórias, como treinamentos, orientações, fiscalização das atividades e fornecimento de equipamentos de proteção individual (EPIs).

"O que vai definir se a empresa agiu com culpa ou negligência e, por consequência, se a família tem o direito de receber indenização ou não", explicou.

O velório e o enterro de Cauã ocorreram na tarde desta terça-feira (26), no Cemitério das Acácias, em Campinas.

Para Bruna Godoy, o filho viveu cada momento e "aproveitou a vida sem arrependimentos".

Bruna destaca o coração generoso, o olhar e o sorriso do filho como marcas da personalidade dele. A mãe descreve Cauã como um jovem alegre, sem maldade e muito amado pela família.

Ele sonhava em ser cantor de trap e chegou a escrever letras, mas não levou o projeto adiante. Para Bruna, o filho viveu os 23 anos intensamente.

“Eu acho que o Cauã sabia que a vida dele ia ser curta aqui na Terra. Por isso que ele viveu intensamente todos esses dias desses 23 anos”, disse.

Segundo a mãe, a filha de Cauã, de 3 anos, era uma das grandes paixões do jovem. “Ele era vidrado nela e ela vidrada nele” , lembra.

“Cauã foi uma luz aqui na Terra”, resume a mãe.

Pessoas próximas também publicaram homenagens a Cauã nas redes sociais. Em uma delas, o jovem foi descrito como um "menino dedicado".

Em uma publicação feita quando Cauã completou 18 anos, Bruna escreveu sobre o orgulho de acompanhar o crescimento do filho e o chamou de "meu filho, meu amigo, meu parceiro, meu confidente" .

"Falar de você pra mim é muito fácil, pois você me transformou em mãe e me fez ver que a vida é linda quando se tem alguém para amar", escreveu.

Na mesma mensagem, Bruna desejou que o filho realizasse os sonhos e fosse feliz.

Cauã Godoy morreu após ser atingido por placas de madeira — Foto: Redes sociais

Segundo apuração da EPTV , afiliada da TV Globo, Cauã retirava placas de madeira quando foi atingido pelo material.

O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado, e o resgate teve o apoio do helicóptero Águia, da Polícia Militar (PM).

Cauã sofreu uma lesão grave na cabeça e teve uma parada cardiorrespiratória. Ele foi levado ao Hospital Municipal Dr. Mário Gatti, mas não resistiu aos ferimentos. A morte foi confirmada pelo hospital.

Jovem fica gravemente ferido após ser atingido por placas de madeira no primeiro dia de trabalho em Campinas — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

articles.title: Idoso internado em Jaú recebe visita de cadela de estimação | G1
articles.standfirst: Reencontro aconteceu no Hospital Amaral Carvalho, em Jaú (SP), com apoio da Ambulância Pet de Mineiros do Tietê. Vínculo entre o aposentado e a cadela se fortaleceu após a morte da esposa dele, que resgatou o animal das ruas.
articles.summary: O reencontro entre o idoso Cícero e sua cadela Joice no Hospital Amaral Carvalho, em Jaú, reforçou o tratamento contra o câncer após 15 dias de saudade.
articles.body:
Dizem que cachorro é o melhor amigo do homem. Para Cícero Ferreira de Melo, de 72 anos, bastou ver Joice entrar pelo corredor do hospital para saber que isso é verdade.

Depois de 15 dias internado no Hospital Amaral Carvalho, em Jaú (SP), o aposentado recebeu a visita de sua cadela de estimação e o encontro emocionou a equipe médica.

Para viabilizar o encontro, a Prefeitura de Mineiros do Tietê (SP), cidade onde o idoso mora, disponibilizou a Ambulância Pet do município para transportar o animal até o hospital. Assista acima ao momento do encontro.

📲 Participe do canal do g1 Bauru e Marília no WhatsApp

Idoso internado no interior de SP recebe visita surpresa de cadela de estimação — Foto: Hospital Amaral Carvalho/Reprodução

Após o período de internação, parte de um tratamento contra o câncer, Cícero já recebeu alta e está em casa ao lado da companheira. Para ele, o momento no hospital renovou suas forças.

"O carinho de um animal desse não tem igual. Foi uma satisfação muito grande. Protejam os animais, porque me corta o coração ver eles sendo judiados", disse o aposentado ao g1.

A cadela chegou à família após ser vítima de maus-tratos. Ela apareceu na rua grávida, assustada e com diversas cicatrizes pelo corpo.

"Apareceu aqui na rua muito arisca e machucada. Ninguém conseguia chegar perto dela. A gente colocava comida, tentava dar água, e ela saía correndo", contou Estela Ferreira de Melo, filha de Cícero, em entrevista ao g1 .

Idoso internado no interior de SP recebe visita surpresa de cadela de estimação — Foto: Prefeitura de Mineiros do Tietê/Divugação

A aproximação só aconteceu quando Joice deu à luz. A esposa de Cícero foi quem acolheu o animal e cuidou dele até a recuperação.

A cadela virou companheira inseparável do idoso, e o vínculo se fortaleceu ainda mais em fevereiro deste ano, quando a esposa de Cícero faleceu.

"Minha mãe acabou indo embora e deixou ela de presente para o meu pai. Virou a companheirinha dele", relata a filha.

Idoso internado no interior de SP recebe visita surpresa de cadela de estimação — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

A liberação da entrada de Joice no hospital passou por uma avaliação criteriosa da equipe multidisciplinar da unidade.

De acordo com o psicólogo hospitalar do Hospital Amaral Carvalho João Paulo Fadini, a presença de animais de estimação traz impactos diretos na recuperação dos pacientes.

"O contato com os animais traz benefícios físicos e emocionais. Fisicamente, promove o bem-estar e a diminuição da pressão arterial, o que ajuda na melhora clínica geral", explica Fadini.

No aspecto emocional, o profissional destaca o ganho em autoestima e segurança.

"O paciente ganha um reforço afetivo muito alto. As visitas são liberadas caso a caso, após análise de médicos, psicólogos, assistentes sociais e enfermagem, garantindo o melhor momento para a saúde do paciente", finaliza o especialista.

articles.title: Piloto sobrevive a queda de avião em MG após acionar paraquedas | G1
articles.standfirst: Gustavo Monteiro Couto, de 29 anos, contou que aeronave perdeu potência durante o voo e que tentou procedimentos de emergência antes de acionar o paraquedas. Piloto recebeu alta do Hospital João XXIII nesta terça-feira (25).
articles.summary: Após alta hospitalar, o piloto Gustavo Monteiro Couto detalha como o uso do paraquedas evitou uma tragédia durante a queda do avião em chamas em Mateus Leme.
articles.body:
O piloto Gustavo Monteiro Couto, de 29 anos, que sobreviveu à queda de um avião monomotor em Mateus Leme, na Grande BH , disse à TV Globo que a aeronave perdeu potência e começou a pegar fogo ainda no ar. Ele acionou o paraquedas do avião antes da queda.

✅ Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 MG no WhatsApp

"Eu tive uma perda de potência. Quando vi que estava tendo algum problema, que não ia ter mais controle da aeronave, tirei a aeronave de cima da cidade de Mateus Leme e procurei um lugar melhor para um pouso de emergência. E aí eu vi que estava pegando fogo e acionei o paraquedas", contou.

Gustavo recebeu alta do Hospital João XXIII, em Belo Horizonte, na tarde desta terça-feira (25). O piloto disse que tentou os procedimentos de emergência para recuperar a potência da aeronave antes de recorrer ao equipamento.

"Eu realizei todos eles para ver se conseguia uma potência novamente. Como não consegui, ele tem esse dispositivo", afirmou.

Gustavo contou que teve medo durante a queda.

"Teme. É ruim, não é um sentimento gostoso, é muito ruim. Toda hora pedindo a Deus para lembrar de todas as coisas que têm que ser feitas e guardar a gente."

Imagens feitas por moradores mostram o avião descendo com o paraquedas acionado e liberando muita fumaça . Depois de atingir o solo, a aeronave foi destruída pelo fogo . Segundo o piloto, a fumaça dentro da cabine dificultou os procedimentos de emergência.

"Eu acredito que o paraquedas me ajudou muito, porque, com a fumaça dentro da cabine, fica difícil você fazer todos os procedimentos. E é nesse momento que eu falei: 'Pô, eu não consigo mais'."

GIF - avião de pequeno porte cai e pega fogo na Grande BH — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Avião de pequeno porte cai e pega fogo na Grande BH — Foto: Reprodução

Gustavo afirmou que só deixou a aeronave depois que ela já estava no chão. Produtores rurais que estavam na região encontraram o piloto consciente. Mateus Macieira, um dos primeiros a chegar ao local, contou que ele pediu água .

"Eu pedi socorro, não porque estava em perigo, mas para poder tomar um gole de água, porque estava doendo a garganta. Me deram, me colocaram no carro e me levaram para a unidade de saúde", disse Gustavo.

Ele foi levado inicialmente para uma unidade de saúde em Serra Azul e, depois, para a UPA de Mateus Leme. Segundo a Polícia Militar, o piloto teve queimadura nas vias aéreas e inalou fumaça. Por precaução, foi transferido para o Hospital João XXIII, em Belo Horizonte.

Aeronave ficou destruida pelo fogo — Foto: Globocop

Na saída do hospital, Gustavo se emocionou ao falar sobre o reencontro com o filho, que completa 2 anos nesta quarta-feira (26).

"Dá vontade de chorar. [...] Dá para ver ele, abraçar, sentir o cheiro dele. E agora viver."

O piloto também agradeceu por ter sobrevivido.

"O sentimento é só de agradecer a Deus por ter dado toda a iluminação e dar tudo certo, a porta estar aberta na hora certa, eu poder respirar, o paraquedas ter funcionado, tudo certo. É só agradecer a Deus mesmo por mim e pela minha família."

A esposa dele, Brenda Monteiro Couto, também falou sobre o momento.

"É um susto que a gente passa, mas acho que a alegria é ainda maior. [...] É uma vida que ele deu novamente para o meu esposo. [...] É o melhor presente que eu poderia ter."

Gustavo Monteiro Couto, de 29 anos, recebeu alta do Hospital João XXIII nesta terça-feira (25) — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Piloto Gustavo Couto de Salles Victor Filho — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

O avião, um Cirrus Design SR22, de prefixo PR-VMI, decolou por volta das 7h45 do Aeroporto da Pampulha, em Belo Horizonte, com destino a Bom Despacho, no Centro-Oeste de Minas. A aeronave caiu no distrito de Serra Azul, em Mateus Leme. Gustavo era o único ocupante.

De acordo com o Registro Aeronáutico Brasileiro (RAB), o avião era de uso particular, estava em situação regular e tinha Certificado de Verificação de Aeronavegabilidade válido até 26 de setembro de 2026. Não havia restrições registradas para a aeronave.

O modelo possui o CAPS (Cirrus Airframe Parachute System), sistema de paraquedas integrado à fuselagem e projetado para reduzir a velocidade da aeronave durante uma situação de emergência .

Segundo a administração do Aeroporto da Pampulha, durante o voo não houve comunicação entre o piloto e a torre de controle relatando emergência, pane ou outra ocorrência.

A Força Aérea Brasileira (FAB) informou que uma equipe do Terceiro Serviço Regional de Investigação e Prevenção de Acidentes Aeronáuticos foi acionada para realizar a ação inicial da ocorrência.
