articles.title: Após sofrer dez facadas no Amazonas, pastor diz que perdoa suspeito | G1
articles.standfirst: Crime aconteceu no município de Maués após vítima ver homem entrar na casa em que mora e tentar roubar itens de um quarto. Mesmo após ter sofrido ferimentos graves, ele diz torcer para agressor mudar de vida.
articles.summary: Crime aconteceu no município de Maués. Mesmo após ter sofrido ferimentos graves, ele diz torcer para agressor mudar de vida.
articles.body:
Pastor e missionário Marcos Rosa sofreu dez facadas durante tentativa de roubo no Amazonas. — Foto: Liam Cavalcante/Rede Amazônica.

O pastor e missionário Marcos Rosa foi ferido com dez golpes de faca durante uma tentativa de roubo dentro da própria casa, no bairro Santa Luzia, em Maués, no interior do Amazonas. Mesmo após o ataque, Marcos afirma que não deseja vingança contra o suspeito e diz que, se tiver a oportunidade de encontrá-lo, pretende perdoá-lo.

Segundo o pastor, o crime aconteceu no dia 16 deste mês, por volta das 3h. Ele estava em casa quando percebeu um homem passando pela vidraça com uma mala e uma chave. O suspeito havia entrado em um dos quartos da residência e estava colocando objetos dentro da mala.

Marcos conseguiu abordar o homem e o manteve no chão enquanto aguardava a chegada da polícia. Durante a espera, porém, o suspeito se levantou e começou a agredi-lo, quando percebeu que o homem estava armado.

📲 Participe do canal do g1 AM no WhatsApp

“Quando eu estava pra imobilizá-lo foi que eu vi a faca na mão dele", relatou.

Marcos foi atacado. Ele conta que tentou se defender, mas não conseguiu evitar os ferimentos. O suspeito fugiu e deixou para trás a faca, um boné e o par de chinelo.

O pastor foi levado ao Hospital Raimunda Francisca Dinelli, em Maués, onde recebeu atendimento. Foi durante o procedimento que ele descobriu a gravidade dos ferimentos.

Segundo Marcos, foram contabilizadas dez perfurações. Duas delas apresentavam maior risco: uma ficou a cerca de um centímetro da jugular e outra atingiu o peito e perfurou o pulmão.

Exames também identificaram pneumotórax e sangramento. O pastor precisou passar por cirurgia e permaneceu internado por cerca de quatro dias para a drenagem do pulmão.

Depois, recebeu alta e iniciou a recuperação em casa. Segundo ele, a recuperação tem sido boa, embora ainda sinta cansaço por causa da lesão no pulmão.

Mesmo diante da violência, Marcos afirma que não deseja o mal ao suspeito. Para ele, o homem deve responder pelo crime dentro da Justiça, mas também pode mudar de vida.

“Meu maior desejo, na verdade, é que essa pessoa mude [...] Eu sei que o Deus que mudou essas pessoas também pode mudar esse jovem.”

O pastor disse que, caso encontre o suspeito, gostaria de conversar com ele e oferecer o perdão.

“Se eu tiver oportunidade é poder abraçar e dizer: 'cara, por mim você está perdoado.'”

A polícia segue investigando o caso e tenta localizar o suspeito. Segundo Marcos, nenhum objeto chegou a ser levado da residência.

articles.title: Empresária morre ao passar por cirurgia plástica na Bahia | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima viajou dos Estados Unidos para a cidade de Ilhéus, no sul da Bahia, para fazer quatro procedimentos. Médico responsável por cirurgia já foi alvo de denúncias.
articles.summary: Vítima viajou dos Estados Unidos para a cidade de Ilhéus, no sul da Bahia, para fazer quatro procedimentos. Médico responsável por cirurgia já foi alvo de denúncias.
articles.body:
Empresária morreu ao passar por cirurgia plástica em Ilhéus — Foto: Redes sociais

Uma empresária de 31 anos morreu ao fazer uma cirurgia plástica em Ilhéus , no sul da Bahia, na madrugada desta quarta-feira (26). Ainda não há informações sobre a causa da morte.

Adriele da Silva Pinto morava nos Estados Unidos e viajou para o Brasil para fazer quatro procedimentos estéticos: mastopexia com prótese, lipoescultura, remodelamento costal e jato de plasma.

Segundo familiares, o médico responsável pelos procedimentos foi o doutor Rossini Tebaldi Ruback, que em 2023 foi alvo de denúncias feitas por pacientes . Na ocasião, diversas mulheres o acusaram de erros e cirurgias mal feitas.

O g1 entrou em contato com a Polícia Civil, com o Conselho Regional de Medicina do Estado da Bahia (Cremeb) e com o Hospital Vida Memorial, onde a cirurgia de Adriele foi feita, e aguarda reposta.

A assessoria de imprensa do médico responsável pelo procedimento informou que encaminhará um posicionamento oficial por escrito.

Segundo o advogado da família, Adriele entrou na cirurgia às 15h de segunda-feira (25) e a cirurgia deveria ser finalizada às 20h. A família foi informada sobre a morte da empresária na madrugada deste terça, após cobrar por notícias sobre a demora do procedimento.

Ainda segundo o advogado, o hospital informou que a paciente passou mal durante a cirurgia e, devido a suspeita dos familiares, um boletim de ocorrência foi registrado na delegacia. Ao ler o relatório médico, o advogado afirmou que o atestado de óbito não foi assinado por Rossini Tebaldi Ruback, médico responsável pela cirurgia.

articles.title: Zema defende novo pacto federativo e diz que prefeito hoje vive 'com pires na mão' | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do Novo à Presidência visitou o Hospital Regional de Teófilo Otoni, no Vale do Mucuri, e afirmou que pretende ampliar a autonomia financeira dos municípios.
articles.summary: Candidato do Novo à Presidência visitou o Hospital Regional de Teófilo Otoni, no Vale do Mucuri, e afirmou que pretende ampliar a autonomia financeira dos municípios.
articles.body:
Romeu Zema (Novo) cumpriu agenda em Teófilo Otoni na manhã desta quarta-feira (26) — Foto: Leonardo Duque/Inter TV dos Vales

O candidato à Presidência da República Romeu Zema ( Novo ) defendeu, nesta quarta-feira (26), durante visita ao Hospital Regional de Teófilo Otoni , no Vale do Mucuri, a criação de um novo pacto federativo para ampliar a participação dos municípios na divisão dos recursos públicos.

Segundo ele, prefeitos enfrentam dificuldades para conseguir verbas e acabam dependentes de repasses e negociações políticas.

“Hoje o problema que nós enfrentamos no Brasil é que o prefeito fica a vida toda com pires na mão pedindo dinheiro.”

A visita ao hospital fez parte da agenda de campanha de Zema no interior de Minas Gerais. Durante a passagem por Teófilo Otoni, o candidato também falou sobre saúde, privatizações, infraestrutura, gastos públicos e citou o caso envolvendo o Banco Master e o Banco de Brasília (BRB).

Questionado sobre investimentos federais na saúde, Zema afirmou que prefere uma mudança na distribuição dos recursos públicos entre União, estados e municípios.

Segundo ele, as prefeituras deveriam receber uma parcela maior das receitas diretamente, sem depender de negociações políticas para obter verbas .

“Ou o governo federal amplia a fatia, ou nós temos de fazer um novo pacto federativo, que é o melhor, na minha opinião, onde os recursos fiquem nas prefeituras.”

O candidato também afirmou que prefeitos são frequentemente pressionados durante períodos eleitorais.

“O que tem de prefeito aí sendo pressionado, chantageado numa época eleitoral por deputados, por senadores. ‘Ah, eu te mando o dinheiro, mas você tem que me apoiar’.”

Durante a visita ao Hospital Regional de Teófilo Otoni, Zema apresentou a unidade como exemplo de investimentos realizados durante os mandatos dele no governo de Minas Gerais.

O candidato afirmou que a principal prioridade de um eventual governo federal seria fortalecer a atenção básica e ampliar o acesso da população às Unidades Básicas de Saúde (UBSs).

Em 2021, Romeu Zema visitou as obras paradas do Hospital Regional de Teófilo Otoni — Foto: Gil Leonardi/Imprensa MG

Segundo ele, a expansão da rede de atendimento primário permite diagnósticos precoces e reduz o agravamento de doenças.

Zema também citou a construção de UBSs em Minas Gerais e afirmou que pretende ampliar esse modelo para o restante do país.

Ao comentar investimentos em infraestrutura, o candidato defendeu a privatização de empresas estatais e afirmou que os recursos poderiam ser direcionados para áreas como saúde e transporte.

“O que eu vou fazer como presidente do Brasil é privatizar as empresas que não geram benefício direto nenhum aos brasileiros e usar esses recursos para colocar essa infraestrutura de pé.”

Ele também afirmou que o poder público deve concentrar esforços em áreas consideradas essenciais.

Durante a defesa das privatizações, Zema citou o caso envolvendo o Banco Master e o Banco de Brasília (BRB).

O candidato utilizou o episódio para criticar a atuação de empresas estatais e defender uma participação maior da iniciativa privada na economia.

“As estatais que estão aí têm sido utilizadas para político fazer politicagem, para cabide de emprego, para corrupção, como nós vimos agora no BRB de Brasília, o banco lá, que foi o único banco que se envolveu com o Banco Master.”

Segundo ele, casos envolvendo empresas públicas acabam gerando prejuízos aos contribuintes.

“As estatais têm sido utilizadas para isso. E quem paga a conta desses escândalos são os brasileiros.”

Ao tratar das contas públicas, o candidato afirmou que pretende combater privilégios e supersalários no serviço público.

Zema também defendeu mais transparência na administração pública e punições mais rígidas para casos de corrupção.

Após a agenda em Teófilo Otoni, Zema segue a campanha em Minas Gerais. A próxima parada do candidato do Novo à Presidência será em São Francisco , no Norte de Minas, onde ele cumpre compromissos de campanha nesta quinta-feira (27).

articles.title: Criança tem pé perfurado e preso em pedal de moto no Amazonas | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente aconteceu no domingo (23), no município de Rio Preto da Eva, enquanto a família se preparava para tomar banho de rio.
articles.summary: Bombeiros foram acionados para remover peça metálica após acidente em Rio Preto da Eva; criança de 4 anos está estável e se recupera bem.
articles.body:
Criança prende o pé em moto no interior do Amazonas — Foto: Divulgação

Uma criança de 4 anos ficou ferida após ter o pé direito perfurado e preso no pedal de uma motocicleta, em Rio Preto da Eva , no interior do Amazonas. O acidente aconteceu no domingo (23), enquanto a família se preparava para tomar banho de rio.

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Amazonas (CBMAM), a equipe foi acionada para retirar a peça metálica que ficou presa ao pé da criança. Para evitar o agravamento do ferimento, os socorristas estabilizaram o membro e usaram uma ferramenta de corte para remover o pedal da motocicleta.

A mãe da criança, que não quis se identificar, contou ao g1 como o acidente aconteceu. "Minha mãe ia levar ele e o irmão para tomar banho de rio e falou para ele ir pegar a sandália dele enquanto ela ia ao banheiro. O meu outro filho disse que ele saiu para ir na casa da vizinha, mas ela não estava. Aí acho que ele viu a moto lá na rua e foi subir e a moto acabou caindo no pé dele porque a rua lá é uma ladeira", relatou.

Após a retirada do pedal, a criança recebeu os primeiros atendimentos ainda no local e foi encaminhada ao Hospital de Rio Preto da Eva.

Segundo a mãe, o menino está estável e se recupera bem.

"Agora ele está bem. Não reclamou de dor. Ontem abriram o curativo e o pezinho não está inchado nem inflamado", disse a mãe.

articles.title: Estudante de medicina morre após acidente de moto no Paraguai | G1
articles.standfirst: Lucas da Silva Mendonça, de 26 anos, foi atingido por uma caminhonete em Pedro Juan Caballero e morreu após ser transferido para Ponta Porã. Ele foi velado em Campo Grande nessa terça-feira (25).
articles.summary: Lucas da Silva Mendonça, de 26 anos, foi atingido por uma caminhonete em Pedro Juan Caballero e morreu após ser transferido para Ponta Porã.
articles.body:
Lucas da Silva Mendonça. — Foto: Rede social.

A Polícia Nacional do Paraguai investiga as circunstâncias do acidente que terminou na morte do estudante de medicina campo-grandense Lucas da Silva Mendonça, de 26 anos. A colisão ocorreu na madrugada do último sábado (22), em Pedro Juan Caballero, cidade paraguaia vizinha de Ponta Porã , em Mato Grosso do Sul.

Lucas pilotava uma motocicleta quando foi atingido pelo motorista de uma caminhonete no cruzamento de uma avenida da cidade fronteiriça. A polícia paraguaia não divulgou informações sobre o condutor da caminhonete que atingiu a vítima.

O rapaz foi sepultado na tarde desta terça-feira (25), em um cemitério de Campo Grande . A cerimônia reuniu familiares, amigos e colegas da faculdade onde ele cursava medicina, no Paraguai.

Após o acidente o estudante foi socorrido pelo Corpo de Bombeiros e encaminhado ao Hospital Regional de Pedro Juan Caballero. Devido à gravidade dos ferimentos, porém, precisou ser transferido para o Hospital Regional de Ponta Porã. Ele morreu na noite de domingo (23).

O corpo de Lucas foi liberado pelo Instituto Médico-Legal (IML) de Ponta Porã na manhã de segunda-feira (24). O velório iniciou no mesmo dia, em Campo Grande.

Em nota, a universidade onde Lucas estudava lamentou a morte do estudante e manifestou solidariedade aos familiares e amigos.

“É com grande tristeza que recebemos a notícia do falecimento de Lucas da Silva Mendonça. Neste momento de dor, nos solidarizamos com todos os familiares e amigos, desejando que encontrem conforto e força para superar essa perda. Que as boas lembranças deixadas por Lucas Mendonça sejam um alento em meio à saudade. Nossos mais sinceros sentimentos a todos que compartilham desta dor. Descanse em paz.”

articles.title: Diretor de Saúde de Piraju é exonerado após mudanças no hospital | G1
articles.standfirst: Exoneração foi confirmada ao g1 pela prefeitura nesta quarta-feira (26). Hospital municipal trocou a empresa terceirizada responsável por administrar o trabalho médico um dia antes da saída do diretor.
articles.summary: O Diretor de Saúde de Piraju foi exonerado após a prefeitura encerrar contrato com a empresa que geria médicos no hospital municipal para reorganizar o pronto-socorro.
articles.body:
Prefeitura de Piraju (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/Google Maps

O diretor de Saúde de Piraju (SP), Osvaldo Sérgio Ortega, foi exonerado do cargo na terça-feira (25). A informação foi confirmada ao g1 pela prefeitura da cidade nesta quarta-feira (26).

Segundo a administração municipal, a substituição, que ocorreu juntamente dos vereadores em uma reunião no gabinete do prefeito, faz parte de uma estratégia para promover melhorias na área da saúde. A assistente social Luana Vendrametto assumirá o cargo temporariamente.

Ainda conforme a prefeitura, a mudança está relacionada à divergências em relação aos objetivos da gestão sobre a saúde municipal. O sucessor definitivo da pasta ainda não foi nomeado.

A exoneração de Osvaldo aconteceu um dia após o hospital municipal não renovar o contrato com a empresa que administrava os serviços médicos na unidade. Por meio de um pronunciamento nas redes sociais, o hospital afirmou que a mudança no quadro de funcionários envolve uma revisão no modelo de atendimentos a pacientes.

"O modelo foi revisto e ajustado para assegurar cobertura adequada do pronto-socorro, dos pacientes internados e das transferências, com uma escala específica para os deslocamento [...] Os desligamentos realizados decorreram de decisões administrativas relacionadas à reorganização do serviço", diz a nota.

O hospital apontou que, além da reorganização interna, houve "dificuldades concretas" para atender pacientes no modelo atual de funcionamento. Em parte do expediente de plantão, os médicos trabalhavam em regime de sobreaviso, ou seja, compareciam ao local apenas quando necessário.

"Respeitamos os profissionais que trabalharam nesse formato, mas a administração avaliou que o modelo não atende plenamente às necessidades. Em alguns momentos, houve dificuldades concretas: profissionais que estavam em atendimento em outras unidades e que nem sempre correspondiam rapidamente aos chamados do pronto atendimento", descreve a nota.

articles.title: 1ª Conferência de Aleitamento Materno é realizada em Macaé | G1
articles.standfirst: Encontro reuniu profissionais da rede de saúde para discutir a criação de um protocolo municipal e fortalecer o atendimento às mães, aos bebês e às famílias.
articles.summary: Encontro reuniu profissionais da rede de saúde para discutir a criação de um protocolo municipal e fortalecer o atendimento às mães, aos bebês e às famílias.
articles.body:
Palestras abordam a importância da amamentação até os seis meses — Foto: Arquivo Secom

Macaé realizou a 1ª Conferência de Promoção do Aleitamento Materno, na Casa da Criança. O encontro teve como principal objetivo avançar na criação de um protocolo municipal de amamentação.

A proposta é organizar e oficializar as orientações, os cuidados e o acolhimento oferecidos às mães, aos bebês e às famílias, além de fortalecer a integração entre a Atenção Básica, o Hospital Público Municipal (HPM) e os demais serviços da rede de saúde.

Durante a conferência, profissionais discutiram políticas públicas voltadas ao aleitamento materno e estratégias para ampliar o apoio às mulheres que amamentam. A programação também abordou as ações desenvolvidas pelo HPM e a contribuição da Atenção Básica para a promoção da amamentação no município.

Evento integra as ações de conscientização do Agosto Dourado — Foto: Arquivo Secom

O encontro faz parte do processo de criação do Comitê Municipal de Aleitamento Materno, que ficará responsável por articular os diferentes níveis de assistência e contribuir para a implantação do protocolo.

A conferência integrou as ações do Agosto Dourado, campanha nacional de conscientização sobre a importância do leite materno para o desenvolvimento e a saúde das crianças.

articles.title: Eleições 2026: Profª Maria do Carmo grava programa eleitoral em Manaus | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidata do PL ao governo do Amazonas gravou, nesta quarta-feira (26), parte de seu programa eleitoral em frente ao Hospital e Pronto-Socorro 28 de Agosto, na zona Centro-Sul de Manaus, e falou sobre propostas para o meio ambiente.
articles.summary: A candidata Maria do Carmo detalhou planos para o meio ambiente e saneamento durante gravação de campanha para as Eleições 2026 em Manaus nesta quarta-feira.
articles.body:
Professora Maria do Carmo grava programa para o horário eleitoral gratuito em frente ao Hospital e Pronto-Socorro 28 de Agosto. — Foto: Marcela Orquiz/g1 AM

A candidata ao governo do Amazonas, Professora Maria do Carmo ( PL ), gravou parte de seu programa para o horário eleitoral gratuito na tarde desta quarta-feira (26). As atividades foram realizadas em frente ao Hospital e Pronto-Socorro 28 de Agosto, na Zona Centro-Sul de Manaus . Durante a atividade, a candidata falou sobre o combate aos lixões na capital e no interior.

Maria do Carmo disputa o cargo pela coligação Mudar é Urgente, formada pelo Partido Liberal (PL) e pelo Partido Novo . A candidata é mestre e doutora em Direito, professora e atua como gestora de instituições de ensino no Amazonas. É a primeira vez que ela concorre ao cargo de governadora.

Perguntada sobre propostas sobre o meio ambiente, Maria do Carmo citou os lixões como o principal problema e caracterizou a questão também como um problema de saúde pública a ser resolvido.

"A principal questão [do meio ambiente no Amazonas] são os lixões, que precisam ser resolvidos. Hoje a gente tem várias oportunidades aí de fazer a questão da reciclagem, de tratar os lixões como aterros sanitários, de fato", declarou Maria do Carmo.

A candidata também pontuou questões relacionadas ao meio ambiente específicas para a capital do estado.

"A gente tem que trabalhar de novo a questão da despoluição dos igarapés; a gente tem um problema seríssimo aqui de arborização, que é uma coisa que demandaria um estudo sério, um censo arbóreo", disse.

A agenda da candidata continou durante a tarde com uma reunião com mães atípicas, um bandeiraço no bairro Coroado com o candidato a deputado federal Sargento Salazar, e uma reunião com apoiadores da Zona Oeste da capital à noite. De manhã, Maria do Carmo participou de um evento do PL em um restaurante no bairro Adrianópolis.

A campanha eleitoral começou no dia 16 de agosto em todo o país. Os candidatos já podem fazer propaganda nas ruas e na internet. Na TV e no rádio, a propaganda começa na sexta-feira (28). O primeiro turno das eleições será no dia 4 de outubro.

articles.title: Tenente da PM morre após teste de aptidão física em Teresina | G1
articles.standfirst: Oficial chegou a ser socorrido com vida, mas faleceu no Hospital de Urgência de Teresina, nesta quarta-feira (26).
articles.summary: O oficial José Luzia da Silva buscava promoção e tinha exames em dia, mas sofreu uma parada cardiorrespiratória após realizar o esforço físico em Teresina.
articles.body:
Tenente da PM morre após infartar depois de teste de aptidão — Foto: Reprodução

O tenente José Luzia da Silva , de 63 anos, faleceu após sofrer um mal súbito na manhã desta quarta-feira (26), em Teresina . De acordo com a Polícia Militar do Piauí, o oficial estava em uma das etapas do Teste de Aptidão Física e, depois, passou mal, foi socorrido e encaminhado ao Hospital de Urgência de Teresina (HUT).

José Luzia chegou a ser atendido com vida, mas não resistiu. O oficial buscava uma promoção dentro da corporação através do TAF. Em nota, a Polícia Militar lamentou o falecimento do tenente.

Segundo a PM, o militar já havia apresentado exames médicos que comprovavam que ele estava apto para a realização do TAF.

Ainda em nota, o órgão afirma que a ocorrência de uma complicação de saúde após esforço físico, isoladamente, não permite estabelecer sua causa ou eventual relação com a realização do TAF

Veja a nota de pesar da Polícia Militar do Piauí:

A Polícia Militar do Piauí informa que, após a realização do Teste de Aptidão Física (TAF), destinado ao processo de promoção de oficiais, o 1º Tenente PM José Luzia da Silva, de 63 anos, apresentou mal-estar súbito enquanto já se encontrava em repouso, evoluindo para uma parada cardiorrespiratória.

Vale ressaltar que a instituição mantém, como parte de seus procedimentos regulares de acompanhamento da saúde e da capacidade funcional de seu efetivo, avaliações periódicas de saúde e de aptidão física, destinadas à verificação das condições necessárias ao desempenho das atribuições inerentes à atividade policial militar. Essas avaliações integram a rotina funcional da Corporação e também são previstas na legislação como requisitos para os processos de promoção na carreira policial militar.

Nesse caso, o militar havia realizado a inspeção periódica de saúde, apresentado todos os exames necessários e encontrava-se regularmente apto, sob o ponto de vista médico-pericial, para a realização do TAF, sem registro de restrição vigente que contraindicasse sua participação.

Uma ambulância do Hospital da Polícia Militar (HPM), com suporte avançado de vida, equipe de saúde e médico, permanecia no local para atendimento de eventuais intercorrências. Após passar mal, o militar recebeu atendimento imediato, com início das manobras de ressuscitação cardiopulmonar e demais medidas de suporte avançado. Em seguida, foi prontamente encaminhado ao Hospital de Urgência de Teresina (HUT), onde foram mantidas as medidas de ressuscitação, infelizmente sem êxito.

A Polícia Militar do Piauí lamenta profundamente o falecimento do oficial e manifesta solidariedade aos familiares, amigos e companheiros de Corporação neste momento de dor. A instituição esclarece ainda que a ocorrência de um evento médico agudo após esforço físico, isoladamente, não permite estabelecer sua causa ou eventual relação com a realização do TAF, dependendo a definição da causa do óbito de elementos clínicos, hospitalares e médico-legais.

A Corporação informa, por fim, que está prestando todo o apoio necessário à família do militar, por meio do Centro de Assistência Integral à Saúde (CAIS) e do Plano de Assistência Funerária (PLANAF).

articles.title: Piloto de asa-delta volta a ser intubado após queda em acidente no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Adilson Schoroeder, de 55 anos, sofreu fratura no fêmur e coágulo na cabeça após atingir veículo. Associação aponta turbulência como provável causa do acidente. Polícia Civil investiga.
articles.summary: Adilson Schoroeder, de 55 anos, sofreu fratura no fêmur e coágulo na cabeça após atingir veículo. Associação aponta turbulência como provável causa do acidente. Polícia investiga.
articles.body:
O piloto de asa-delta Adilson Schoroeder , de 55 anos, precisou ser novamente intubado após apresentar piora no estado clínico, segundo o Hospital Nossa Senhora das Graças, de Canoas na noite desta terça-feira (25).

Ele está internado desde o acidente sofrido no domingo (23) , em Sapiranga , na Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre . Durante uma manobra de pouso no Morro Ferrabraz, ele caiu sobre um carro que passava pela rua.

Conforme a atualização médica, Schoroeder teve rebaixamento do nível de consciência e instabilidade, o que levou ao retorno da ventilação mecânica. Ele está em um leito de unidade de terapia intensiva (UTI).

O piloto havia permanecido mais de 24 horas sem intubação, mas a equipe médica decidiu retomar o suporte respiratório após a reavaliação do quadro. Ele seguirá acompanhado pelas equipes clínica e de traumatologia.

Considerado um dos nomes mais experientes do voo livre no Rio Grande do Sul, Schoroeder chegou a sair do coma induzido na segunda-feira (24) .

Nos últimos dias, ele realizou exames de imagem e passou por uma cirurgia em decorrência de uma fratura no fêmur. O paciente foi diagnosticado com um coágulo na cabeça e sangue no pulmão.

VEJA: Vídeo mostra decolagem de piloto de asa-delta que ficou ferido em acidente

Adilson Schoroeder mora em São Leopoldo e trabalha produzindo doces e salgados para festas e tem o voo de asa-delta como sua paixão. Com 15 anos de experiência, o piloto se interessou pelo esporte ainda na infância, quando se mudou para Sapiranga.

"Ele fala que aos oito anos veio pra Sapiranga e viu uma asa-delta. Desde então, é o sonho dele", conta o filho, Alan Schoroeder.

A dedicação do piloto chama a atenção de Alex Trombini, presidente da Associação Gaúcha de Voo Livre (AGVL), por ele dedicar tanto tempo ao esporte, inclusive durante a semana, conciliando com as atividades de trabalho. "Talvez o piloto em atividade que mais voa em números de voo, pois voa em alguns dias da semana."

Agora, a família aguarda pela recuperação. "Ele já era um piloto bom. Depois do acidente, vai sair um piloto ainda melhor", destaca o filho.

A Polícia Civil instaurou um inquérito para investigar o acidente . "Não houve perícia no local. Serão ouvidas testemunhas. Pelo que temos até o momento não há crime, mas as causas possíveis do acidente serão investigadas", diz o delegado Clóvis Nei da Silva.

Segundo a AGVL, a provável causa do acidente foi uma turbulência na asa-delta no momento final do pouso . "Isso fez com que a asa fosse para o lado aumentando a velocidade e não conseguiu mais segurar", explica o presidente da associação.

O presidente relata que as árvores de grande porte localizadas na proximidade da área de pouso são um desafio para os pilotos.

"Não tinha mais espaço para corrigir a curva e nem altura para fazer a curva para a direita. Acabou fazendo a curva para a direita, que era a opção menos ruim que ele tinha, colidiu contra a asa na vegetação e caiu no asfalto", diz.

articles.title: Poste desaba e fere mulher e criança em Copacabana, na Zona Sul do Rio | G1
articles.standfirst: Estrutura caiu sobre as vítimas na Avenida Nossa Senhora de Copacabana. As duas foram levadas ao Hospital Municipal Miguel Couto e não correm risco de vida.
articles.summary: Após o poste cair em Copacabana, as vítimas foram levadas ao Hospital Miguel Couto com ferimentos, mas estão fora de perigo segundo a Secretaria de Saúde.
articles.body:
Um poste desabou sobre uma mulher e uma criança na noite de terça-feira (25), em Copacabana, na Zona Sul do Rio. As vítimas foram socorridas e levadas para o Hospital Municipal Miguel Couto.

O acidente aconteceu na Avenida Nossa Senhora de Copacabana, na altura da Rua Dias da Rocha, e foi registrado por câmeras de segurança da região. Após a queda da estrutura metálica, a área foi interditada.

Segundo testemunhas, a mulher, de cerca de 35 anos, e a criança, de 5, caminhavam de mãos dadas quando foram atingidas. O local fica próximo a um ponto de ônibus de grande movimento.

“Eu estava no meu local de trabalho, tinha acabado de chegar e só escutei um barulho. Muita gente começou a correr. Nesse momento, vi a estrutura no chão, e a moça e a criança estavam feridas”, contou Adilson Miranda, porteiro de um prédio em frente ao local do acidente.

Moradores e pedestres prestaram os primeiros socorros até a chegada dos bombeiros, que atenderam as vítimas em menos de 15 minutos. O atendimento inicial foi feito na calçada antes da remoção para o hospital.

“Já estava toda corroída por baixo, podre. A qualquer hora isso ia acontecer”, afirmou Adilson sobre a estrutura.

De acordo com a Secretaria Municipal de Saúde, a mulher sofreu ferimentos moderados e permanece internada em estado estável. A criança teve ferimentos leves. As duas estão fora de perigo.

A RioLuz informou que o equipamento era um armário óptico pertencente a uma empresa de telecomunicações. Uma equipe foi enviada ao local e realizou a retirada da estrutura, que apresentava risco à segurança dos pedestres.

articles.summary: Menina atingida por bala perdida em Sapiranga passou por cirurgia para retirar projétil do braço após incidente no bairro 7 de Setembro; polícia investiga o caso.
articles.body:
Uma menina de 10 anos foi atingida por uma bala perdida enquanto brincava em um pula-pula na tarde de sábado (22) , em Sapiranga , no Vale do Sinos. A polícia investiga de onde partiu o disparo.

Segundo as autoridades, a criança teria sentido uma ardência no braço e foi encaminhada para atendimento médico no Hospital Sapiranga. A paciente foi submetida a um exame de raio-x, que apontou o projétil alojado no antebraço direito .

A menina passou por procedimento cirúrgico e a bala foi retirada . Conforme a polícia, testemunhas que estavam no local do incidente relataram que não ouviram barulho de tiros.

articles.title: Acidente no Paraná: Duas mulheres morrem em batida com caminhão | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítimas, de 58 e 59 anos, estavam no carro com os maridos, que ficaram feridos. Acidente aconteceu entre Francisco Beltrão e Enéas Marques.
articles.summary: Acidente no Paraná entre Francisco Beltrão e Enéas Marques vitimou duas cunhadas que voltavam para casa com os maridos em uma colisão frontal com caminhão.
articles.body:
Duas mulheres, que eram cunhadas, morreram após o carro em que estavam bater de frente com um caminhão na rodovia que liga Francisco Beltrão a Enéas Marques , no Sudoeste do Paraná.

Delaide Baggio Borghezan, de 59 anos, morreu no local. A outra vítima, Rozinei Alberton Borghesan, de 58 anos, foi socorrida e levada ao Hospital Regional, mas não resistiu aos ferimentos e morreu posteriormente.

As duas estavam no carro com os respectivos maridos, que também ficaram feridos. Segundo familiares, os dois irmãos e suas esposas voltavam para casa quando se envolveram no acidente.

As vítimas morreram no acidente de trânsito — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Os dois homens foram encaminhados para atendimento médico e permanecem internados, mas, segundo a família, estão fora de risco. A identidade deles não foi divulgada.

A dinâmica da batida e as causas do acidente serão apuradas pela perícia.

articles.title: NHS failing child sex abuse victims, say psychiatrists
articles.summary: There have been decades of mistreatment and mismanagement of those who seek help later in life, say experts in a new, damning report.
articles.body:
People sexually abused as children who seek help in later life for mental health problems are being failed by the NHS, senior doctors have told the BBC.

The Royal College of Psychiatrists is issuing a public apology for what is says is decades of mismanagement and misdiagnosis in the UK.

For some, it has worsened their traumas, it said.

The college said mental health staff have been too focussed on treating symptoms rather than exploring how past traumatic experiences can still affect patients.

Support is improving, it said, but there must be better training and more investment. One of the biggest problems is services have too little time to spend with these patients, it adds.

The apology has been included in a report by the college and given to the BBC.

Author and immediate past president of the college, Dr Lade Smith, said she was "sorry" that, too often, victims have suffered "avoidable harm when seeking help".

The report details how treatment has sometimes been inappropriate, while people have been re-traumatised by the experience of repeated assessments and history-taking and not always being believed.

Dr Smith told the BBC it was clear people were not getting the support they needed, and that this was not just a failing of psychiatrists, but the whole mental health system.

"Services are so fragmented. The system is set up to provide short, discreet episodes of care. Psychiatrists do not get the time to build up a relationship with patients so they can be properly supported.

"They are lucky if they get eight sessions of therapy, when it could take eight sessions for a person just to disclose the abuse.

"And these are just the people who get support â many don't even get seen by mental health services because services are so stretched," she said.

Estimates suggest nearly one in 10 adults in England and Wales were abused in childhood.

Such trauma increases the risk of mental health problems, including alcohol and drug misuse, eating disorders, self-harm, complex PTSD, anxiety and depression.

Many struggle to talk about the abuse. Around two-thirds of those abused as children have not disclosed it to services by the time they reach adulthood.

One in five never disclose, and many of those that do take decades to speak out.

Caroline Thompson, 65, is someone who feels let down by the NHS.

She was psychologically and sexually abused when she was a child.

She went on to raise a family and have a successful career as a specialist ear, nose and throat doctor.

It was not until she started experiencing terrifying nightmares, aged 55, that left her unable to function due to mental exhaustion and lack of sleep, that she realised she needed help and was referred to mental health services.

The psychiatrist she saw said her symptoms were unlikely to be due to the abuse because of the delay in presentation and given she had been able to have a family and successful career. She was diagnosed with anxiety and given anti-psychotic drugs.

"I had therapy for about a year and was then discharged. At that point I still didn't understand what was happening to me and I still couldn't function due to the nightmares and side-effects of the drugs. I had to give up the job I loved."

Caroline then got private therapy with a therapist who specialised in childhood trauma and gradually began to get better over the next few years.

She says: "It was astonishing to me that it was not understood that traumatic memories are buried in order for you to survive, and that those memories can surface years later. So any delay in presenting is quite normal."

The apology comes after the college set up a working group of experts, doctors and abuse survivors, including Caroline, to review NHS care.

The group was set up after mental health services have seen a rise in people coming forward seeking help in the last decade or so, following high-profile abuse scandals involving schools, children's homes and religious institutions, as well as the Jimmy Savile crimes .

The college is calling for a number of changes. It is promising to develop specialist training materials for psychiatrists, but wants mandatory training for all mental health staff on the importance of trauma-informed care for survivors of child sex abuse.

And it has recommended national guidance be published on how to recognise and respond to disclosures of historic child sex abuse, as well as an overhaul of services so those needing help can get the long-term support they need.

Gabrielle Shaw, chief executive of the National Association for People Abused in Childhood, said this was a "significant and welcome" apology, but it must lead to "meaningful change".

"For too many adult survivors, mental health services have not felt like a route to safety or recovery.

"They have been another place where the impact of trauma was missed or where the offered treatment was inappropriate."

She said some are met with disbelief which can be particularly "damaging", while even when the trauma is recognised others are told they are "too complex, unsuitable or outside the remit of available services."

A spokesman for NHS England said victims could access support 24 hours a day, seven days a week through sexual assault referral centres and counselling services with information about them available on the NHS website , external .

"People who have suffered historic child sexual abuse may not have spoken about it for years, so it's vital they know they can access specialist, trauma-informed support through the NHS," he added.

He also said steps were being taken to better support children and young people with additional training being provided to mental health support teams in schools and colleges.

If you've been affected by the issues in this story, you can find information, advice and support from the BBC's Action Line . Anyone feeling emotionally distressed or suicidal can call Samaritans for free on 116 123 or visit samaritans.org in the UK.

articles.title: At least 15 newborns killed in Pakistan hospital fire
articles.summary: Only one child rescued after fire breaks out in the nursery at Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences, Geo News reports.
articles.body:
A fire has broken out in the children’s ward at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) Hospital in Islamabad, killing at least 15 newborns, according to local media.

Geo News, citing hospital officials, reported on Wednesday that the nursery at PIMS housed 16 newborns at the time of the incident.

The outlet cited officials as saying the fire started after an air conditioner compressor exploded in the nursery.

The blaze has been extinguished, and firefighters are carrying out cooling operations at the site, it added.

articles.title: Dorset and Hampshire 1976 heatwave was 'like a war zone'
articles.summary: As another hot summer prompts comparisons with 1976, people say the memories remain vivid.
articles.body:
People who lived through the heatwave of 1976 have said memories of the flames, intense heat and fear remain as vivid today as they were 50 years ago.

Dorset and Hampshire residents, firefighters and police officers recalled fast-moving blazes that threatened a fuel depot, forced a hospital evacuation and left communities on edge.

The 1976 heatwave saw 15 consecutive days of temperatures exceeding 32C, and comparisons have been made between the UK's recent high temperatures and the heatwave 50 years ago.

Many said they could still remember sleepless nights, the smell of smoke and uncertainty over what might happen next.

Former retained firefighter Mike Briggs said: "It was just like a war zone. It was so intense, you couldn't fight it."

At one point a fire approached St Leonards Hospital near Ringwood in Dorset.

Former police officer Graham Walbrin said evacuating the hospital was an unprecedented step.

"It was totally unheard of, the fact you evacuate the hospital with elderly people and beds and everything else," he said.

"The trauma for the patients being turfed out of their beds and moved out in the middle of the road."

The scale of the danger became clear when flames approached West Moors and a major nearby fuel depot.

Geoff, who was 11 at the time, said: "I remember the BBC national news, it was the headline article saying something like fire threatens NATO's largest petroleum dump in Europe.

He recalled people being told to leave their homes as crews raced to protect the site.

Briggs said firefighters eventually had to force their way inside.

"We just got in there and it [the fire] was licking around the tanks with thousands of gallons of fuel," he said.

Another firefighter remembered fearing the consequences if the tanks had not been full and had vapour in them that could ignite.

"Thankfully, they were full," he said. "But I was glad to leave that site that day."

Within the past month wildfires have scorched southern England.

According to Reading University's Atmospheric Observatory, by mid-July, more days had reached at least 30C in the summer than in 1976, which was previously the benchmark for hot summers.

It said five of this year's 15 days were in the top 20 highest temperatures ever recorded at the university since it started collecting data in 1908.

Prof Andrew Charlton-Perez, from the university, said: "For half a century, 1976 was the benchmark every hot summer got measured against. Now 2026 has taken its place."

Half a century on, those who lived through the summer of 1976 said the memories had never really faded.

"It doesn't seem 50 years ago because you remember it quite vividly," said resident Ian Knight.

"It was a scary time for people that remember it back in '76.

"A lot of people were genuinely frightened, you know, to go to bed at night."

And Knight said the smell lingered long after the flames had been extinguished.

"We were told, keep your windows shut. The smell of the fire just lingered for weeks."

Months of hot, dry weather helped create conditions for a series of major fires, stretching emergency services and threatening communities across Dorset and Hampshire.

Briggs recalled facing flames that were impossible to control.

"It was just a wall of flame," he said. "It was crowning in the tops of the trees."

As crews battled multiple blazes, local people were asked to help, and Knight said police approached him and his friends to assist firefighters.

"They said, 'Have you got any spare time?'" he recalled. "'The fire brigade are really stretched'."

The group were handed fire beaters and spent hours helping tackle small outbreaks.

The effects were felt by firefighters' families too.

Dawn, whose husband Dave was among those tackling the blazes, said: "All the bedding stank, everything.

"Although he showered, it still smelt. It was absolutely awful. It was just non-stop, every single day," she added.

articles.title: Solihull mum's perforated bowel ordeal after scan error
articles.summary: Mum developed sepsis after scan error and now calls for better postnatal care for women.
articles.body:
"No-one should have to go through what I did after having a baby," said Natalie Chubb after a harrowing post-birth ordeal.

On 11 January 2023, she welcomed her baby girl into the world by caesarean section at Birmingham's Good Hope Hospital, but the newborn bliss soon turned sour and she was left needing emergency surgery for a perforated bowel.

"I knew something wasn't right after Brooke was born, but it felt like my concerns weren't being taken seriously," the 37-year-old from Solihull said.

A University Hospitals Birmingham spokesperson said the Trust "is committed to providing safe, high-quality care" to all patients and to "learning from when things do not go as expected."

Just days after the birth, she began to suffer severe pain and swelling in her abdomen but says her symptoms were downplayed.

As well as debilitating pain, she also suffered vomiting, which included faecal matter, but on 14 January, doctors misinterpreted her scan as showing temporary slowing of her bowel's movements following surgery, medical negligence lawyers at Irwin Mitchell said.

"My condition got worse over several days. Being told I needed emergency surgery is something I'll never forget. I was frightened I might die," the factory worker added.

Despite raising concerns, her condition deteriorated and she developed sepsis. On 18 January, she underwent emergency surgery, in which part of her bowel was removed and a stoma fitted.

The Trust admitted admitted a breach of duty and that a CT scan carried out four days earlier was incorrectly reported.

Decisions about Natalie's care were based on that error, the Trust has said.

"As legal discussions are ongoing, it would not be appropriate to comment on the detail of the case, however, we are working constructively with [Natalie's] representatives."

The mother, who also has a 15-year-old son, explained: "The impact on my life has been huge and I still live with the effects. I continue to struggle with pain, fatigue and digestive problems. It's affected everything from being able to do daily tasks to how I've been able to care for Brooke and Callum."

Natalie is now campaigning for women to receive better care following childbirth and to ensure their concerns are heard.

She added: "I just want other women to be listened to and for warning signs after birth not to be missed."

Jade Elliott-Archer, of Irwin Mitchell, said: "Our investigations have identified concerning failings in how Natalie's condition was recognised and responded to as her condition worsened.

"While these admissions provide Natalie with answers she deserves, they also highlight serious concerns about the care women can receive after birth."

Natalie has since had further surgery, including reversal of the stoma and treatment for complications including a hernia and ongoing wound problems.

"If my experience helps improve care for even one mum, then it will have been worth it," she said.

articles.title: Sara Martín Barbell, doctora: "Llegó una chica de 22 años con convulsiones por dos cosas que hacen millones de mujeres..."
articles.standfirst: No sabemos muchas veces el riesgo que corremos
articles.summary: No sabemos muchas veces el riesgo que corremos
articles.body: En ocasiones, tenemos tan incorporadas nuestras cotumbres y hábitos que no nos damos cuenta del impacto que tienen en nuestro organismo. Y es, de esta manera, como corremos un riesgo excepcional. Es el caso que narra Sara Marín, médico y divulgadora de temas de salud, en su cuenta de tik tok @uncafecontudoctora. En su anécdota cuenta cómo una chica de 22 años llegó a urgencias convulsionando por dos cosas que hacen millones de chicas y que pueden tener un riesgo muy alto sin que las mujeres nos demos cuenta.  En la historia real que cuenta la especialista, la chica finalmente padece un trombohemolismo pulmonar bilateral, es decir, coágulos en ambos pulmones con tan solo 22 años. Además, cuando estaba convulsionando le hicieron una resonancia cerebral y se pudo ver que, a esa corta edad, estaba padeciendo un ictus. Pero, ¿qué puede llevar a una mujer tan joven el atravesar estas enfermedades o patologías tan súmamente graves? La especialista señala que son dos cosas las que llevaron a esta mujer a sufrir este horrible panorama médico. Una combinación de dos hábitos que no se tienen en cuenta y que generan problemas graves en las féminas. Esta chica tomaba pastillas anticonceptivas y vapeaba. Esta combinación pudo ser la clave por la que casi pierde la vida, ya que en este caso, no existían patologías previas relacionadas con esta cuestión. Este, lejos de ser un caso aislado, es uno bastante común y corriente entre muchas mujeres. Según la especialista casi la mitad de las mujeres de entre 18 años y 30 han vapeado alguna vez. Pero, si además se consumen pastillas anticonceptivas, el problema es aún mayor. La pastilla anticonceptiva que lleva trógeno lo que hace que tu sangre se vuelva más espesa y propensa a formar coágulos. No quiere decir que por tomar la pastilla vayas a tener un trombo, pero si le sumas la nicotina aumentan las posibilidades exponencialmente.  Muchos os preguntaréis si el problema es la nicotina, por qué no hay tantos problemas con el tabaco. La especialista lo deja claro: "un cigarrillo puede durar cinco o diez minutos y se acaba, por lo que tu cuerpo descansa hasta el siguiente. El vaper no acaba." De hecho, hay vapers que tienen tantas pulsaciones como el equivalente a 600 cigarros. Dejar de fumar puede mejorar tu salud pero, abandonar el vaper, puede salvar directamente tu vida. Es una decisión crucial, incluso, si eres joven.

articles.title: Eating less of common ingredient early in life may slash cancer risk decades later
articles.summary: Researchers found that early-life sugar rationing in post-war Britain correlated with lower cancer risk and slower aging roughly 50 years later.
articles.body: Limiting sugar consumption during the first 1,000 days of life, from conception through a child’s second birthday, may result in slower biological aging and a lower risk of cancer up to five decades later. A study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences investigated how early-life sugar intake influences health in adulthood, examining data from over 64,000 participants in the UK Biobank born between 1951 and 1956. The researchers leveraged a natural experiment from post-war Britain, when sugar rationing ended in September 1953. DIRTY SODA DRINKS ARE EVERYWHERE, BUT DOCTORS WARN OF HEALTH RISKS: 'METABOLIC DISASTER' After rationing ended, average daily sugar consumption across the U.K. nearly doubled — from about 41 grams to 80 grams — while consumption of other major foods remained stable, according to historical National Food Survey data cited in the study. People exposed to sugar rationing during their first 1,000 days of life were compared to those who were conceived after the policy ended. Researchers then examined cancer outcomes recorded about five decades later. They found that people who spent more of their early lives under sugar rationing had lower rates of several cancers in adulthood, including liver, rectal, lung, prostate and breast cancers. People exposed to early sugar limits also had longer leukocyte telomeres — protective caps on chromosomes that tend to shorten with age — equivalent to about two fewer years of biological aging. They also had lower levels of Granzyme B, a protein associated with long-term immune activation and inflammation. EATING COMMON DAIRY FOOD EVERY DAY MAY SLOW BIOLOGICAL AGING, STUDY SUGGESTS The study’s authors identified two key pathways that could explain these long-term benefits: a biological imprint and a persistent behavioral habit. Five decades after rationing ended, adults who spent their earliest days under sugar restrictions were still consuming less sugar and eating healthier, more varied diets. Experts said the findings add to ongoing research into how early diet may influence long-term health, though further research is needed to confirm the connection. "What surprised me most was how persistent the effects were," study author Weilong Zhang of the University of Cambridge told Fox News Digital. POPULAR DAILY DRINKING HABIT COULD NEARLY TRIPLE RISK OF DEADLY CANCER, MAJOR STUDY FINDS "We might expect childhood diet to matter for health, but differences in sugar exposure during just the first 1,000 days were still reflected in people's diets and biological markers roughly five decades later." "This suggests that early life may be an especially important period not only for biological development, but also for establishing long-lasting food preferences." Dr. Brian Slomovitz, deputy director of the Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center at Mount Sinai Medical Center in Miami Beach, described the research as an "excellent hypothesis-generating study." "Sugar consumption is something that we have been worrying about ... most importantly, inflammation, and how inflammation can lead to some cancers," Slomovitz, who was not involved in the study, told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES High sugar intake has been linked to metabolic disruption, insulin resistance and chronic inflammation, which may contribute to disease risk, according to Dr. Marc Siegel, senior medical analyst for Fox News. Siegel said the lower cancer rates were consistent with the possibility that less early sugar exposure and healthier later-life diets played a role. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER However, outside oncologists note that natural experiments from decades past come with inherent research limitations. "We're talking about the 1950s, so clearly there are some biases in data collection," Slomovitz noted. "Secondly, the numbers are very, very, very low. Of all the cancers, most of them had [fewer] than 100 cases ... to show a 70% decrease, I think is probably an ambitious conclusion." The doctor also pointed out that while obesity-driven cancers align with metabolic pathways, other findings in the paper — such as reduced lung cancer risk — are traditionally tied to external factors like smoking rather than dietary sugar. The researchers noted that, as a natural experiment rather than a randomized trial, the study could not rule out all other postwar factors. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Additionally, the UK Biobank is not fully representative of the broader British population, and the researchers could not determine how much of the effect reflected early biological changes versus healthier diets maintained in adulthood. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Zhang cautioned against overinterpreting the findings as a reason for extreme dietary measures. "I would not interpret our study as saying that parents should eliminate sugar completely," he said. "Rather, our findings support existing recommendations to limit added sugar, particularly during pregnancy and early childhood."

articles.title: Locked inside: Grief and anger as Pakistan hospital fire kills 14 newborns
articles.summary: A nursery for critical infants — supposedly the safest place in Islamabad’s PIMS hospital — turned into a deathtrap.
articles.body:
Islamabad, Pakistan — It was 6:30am on Wednesday when Arif Rana, 46, woke to a phone call. He had been asleep on the lawn outside the maternity unit of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), Islamabad’s largest public-sector hospital.

“My sister gave birth to a baby girl on Tuesday, and she was admitted in the general ward of the hospital. The call came from her husband’s sister, who was attending to my sister, yelling and asking me to come up as a fire had erupted inside the ward,” he told Al Jazeera.

Rana and his 20-year-old son, who was also with him at the hospital, rushed into the ward barefoot. They encountered smoke billowing from the building. As they climbed to the third floor, they found the corridors pitch-black and suffocatingly hot.

“It was hot, and I could hear so much yelling and panicked shouts, and I couldn’t even see due to darkness,” Rana recalled, sitting outside the ward hours after the incident. “The smoke made it hard to breathe.”

He found his sister’s mother-in-law inside the ward and took her to safety. Outside, he found his sister and her newborn, who had been rescued by his sister-in-law.

“It was only due to her [the sister-in-law’s] courage and bravery that my sister, her newborn survived, otherwise, they too could have died in there,” he said quietly, just as 14 other newborns had, in the hospital’s critical care nursery down the corridor.

According to hospital management, the fire was caused by a short circuit in the nursery’s air-conditioning unit. The nursery had 15 newborns in it at the time. Only one was rescued.

It was not the first time a fault in hospital air conditioning has killed newborns in Pakistan.

In June 2024, a similar fire tore through the paediatric ward of Sahiwal Teaching Hospital in Punjab province, killing 11 babies.

Punjab’s Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, the niece of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, later ordered the arrest of the hospital’s medical superintendent and three senior doctors after inquiries found that the hospital’s fire extinguishers had expired.

Accounts of exactly when rescuers reached the ward on Wednesday differ.

A statement from the Islamabad district administration put the first emergency call at 6:45am, with fire tenders and ambulances reaching the hospital within seven minutes.

An official at the headquarters of Rescue 1122 — the government-run ambulance, fire and rescue service — told Al Jazeera that separate stations logged fires at different times as calls were relayed.

His own station received word at 6:55am and reached the hospital less than 10 minutes later. A video he recorded on arrival, which he later showed Al Jazeera, was timestamped 7:06am.

“When we tried to enter the building, it was inaccessible and we could see smoke coming out from the building. We had to break the concrete grills, behind which were windows. We had to break those windows, and through them we were able to rescue people,” a fireman told Al Jazeera on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to speak to the media.

Kamran Riaz, from Rawalpindi, was also at the hospital, holding his five-year-old nephew in his lap. Some 50 metres away, Riaz’s elder brother — and the nephew’s father — was in the hospital morgue, submitting a DNA sample. The brother’s baby daughter, born only three days earlier, was among the 14 who died in the fire. She had been admitted to the nursery because of breathing problems.

“We have no clarity on what is going on, and what we need to do now,” Riaz said. “But from what little my brother told me, there was little to no staff presence in the morning when fire broke out, and there was only one entrance and exit, while the second one was blocked.”

Several witnesses with relatives admitted to different wards in the maternity unit described a similar experience.

The Mother and Child Hospital at PIMS has two wings, one older and one newly constructed.

The fire broke out on the third floor of the older wing, which has one main entrance and exit. The emergency exits, witnesses said, were blocked from inside.

Several people at the hospital told Al Jazeera that renovation work had been under way somewhere inside the building in recent weeks, although no one could provide details about its scope or location.

Samina Waqar, 30, had also spent the night at the hospital with her sister, who had given birth by caesarean section the previous day.

“My brother-in-law wanted to go and see his wife, and when he tried to go there in the morning, that is when he heard the screaming and yelling, and he called me immediately about the fire,” she told Al Jazeera.

Waqar said she ran towards the ward to help with the rescue. Her sister, despite having undergone surgery the previous day, managed to walk out on her own, while her brother-in-law carried the newborn to safety.

“Our ward was right across the nursery where fire broke out, and the entire floor was full of smoke and heat. I don’t even know how we managed to bring them back, along with few other new mothers. It was all a blur for me,” she said.

The wife of Sardar Atee Rehman, 39, was also among those in the ward next to the nursery after giving birth to a daughter the previous day.

“My wife called me around 6.30am in the morning, yelling that there is a fire somewhere and smoke is filling up her ward, and asked me to rush inside,” he said.

Rehman said the security staff inside had been helpful, but he was unable to spot any nurses or a doctor. Several other witnesses made similar observations.

Some relatives later said hospital staff had been present overnight but fled when the fire broke out, which some described as a natural reaction to panic.

PIMS’s administration gave a different account.

The hospital’s executive director, Rana Imran Sikandar, said two doctors and four nurses had been on duty in the intensive care unit when the fire began.

Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry, speaking to reporters at the hospital, repeated the same figures.

Abdul Ghaffoor, a 26-year-old from Rawalpindi who was attending to his mother, said he saw the commotion outside the ward and ran for help.

“I heard that staff keeps the exits and doors locked because it is a maternity ward and they want to ensure that men are not allowed, while also there have been numerous cases of baby stealing, and that is why the staff keeps exits locked,” he said.

PIMS officials gave reporters much the same explanation.

Access to the nursery was restricted, they said, as part of a longstanding policy intended to prevent infants from being stolen from the ward, rather than a lapse specific to Wednesday’s fire.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ordered an investigation into the fire and later suspended the federal health secretary, Aslam Ghaury.

Two separate inquiry committees, one formed by the Islamabad district administration and another by the prime minister’s office, have been tasked with determining what went wrong.

Waqar, whose sister survived the ordeal, was furious with the hospital administration, blaming it for negligence and failing to provide adequate protection for patients, particularly newborns.

“This is a nursery for critical infants, if one place had to have most immediate attention for safety, it was this room, and yet the criminal attitude led to this tragedy,” she said.

articles.title: Delhi reports 138 fresh H1N1 cases in 24 hours; tally crosses 2,400
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi reported 138 new H1N1 cases in the last 24 hours, taking the cumulative number of cases this year to 2,446, the Delhi government said.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi reported 138 new H1N1 cases in the last 24 hours, taking the cumulative number of cases this year to 2,446, the Delhi government said on Wednesday.The total number of Influenza-A cases has now reached 3,177 as the city continues to see a rise in seasonal influenza infections, news agency PTI reported.The latest figures come hours after the Delhi Medical Association advised residents to remain cautious amid the increase in H1N1 cases.The association has urged people to wear masks in crowded places, avoid unnecessary exposure and seek medical advice instead of self-medicating.Hospitals asked to strengthen preparednessHealth minister Pankaj Kumar Singh held a virtual review meeting with medical directors and medical superintendents of Delhi government hospitals to assess preparedness for H1N1, seasonal influenza and other respiratory illnesses.The minister directed hospitals to strengthen emergency services and ensure adequate availability of isolation beds, doctors, testing facilities, medicines and other essential resources.Hospitals have been asked to maintain at least five isolation beds. Larger hospitals have been directed to keep 10 or more beds for managing influenza and vector-borne disease cases.They have also been instructed to maintain shift-wise duty rosters and ensure round-the-clock availability of doctors and medical staff, PTI reported.Dedicated flu corners at hospitalsThe health department has directed hospitals to establish or strengthen dedicated flu corners in emergency departments.Senior residents are to be deployed for emergency duty, while suspected patients should be assessed promptly. Swab samples should also be collected and sent for testing wherever clinically indicated.Hospitals have been asked to maintain adequate stocks of Viral Transport Medium and other supplies needed for respiratory specimen collection and testing.Special emphasis has been placed on children and elderly patients. Hospitals have been directed to ensure their timely assessment and appropriate care.DMA urges masks, no self-medicationThe Delhi Medical Association has advised people with flu-like symptoms to wear N95 masks and avoid meeting relatives, friends and others to reduce the risk of transmission.It has also advised people to maintain respiratory and hand hygiene, avoid crowded places and cover their mouth and nose while coughing or sneezing.The association has cautioned against taking antibiotics or antiviral medicines without consulting a qualified doctor.People returning from areas reporting increased influenza activity have also been advised to monitor their health for at least 10 days and seek medical attention if symptoms develop.‘No need for panic’: Health minister“There is no need for panic. Most of the patients who have come to hospitals so far have presented with mild fever and other common symptoms and have recovered within a day or two,” Singh said.He said Delhi government hospitals were fully prepared, and the health system was continuously monitoring the situation, PTI reported.“This was not merely a meeting to issue instructions, but a comprehensive review of the preparedness of our hospitals,” he said.Singh said the availability of beds, testing facilities, medicines and emergency services had been reviewed to ensure there was no gap in patient care.He also appealed to people to remain vigilant without panicking and follow respiratory hygiene, hand hygiene and cough etiquette.The minister advised people to use masks appropriately and avoid unnecessary exposure to crowded places, particularly when symptomatic.The health department will continue to monitor influenza trends and hospital preparedness, with a focus on timely testing, adequate isolation capacity, essential medicines and uninterrupted emergency services.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: FDA approves ‘game-changing’ pancreatic cancer drug
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration on Wednesday approved a groundbreaking pancreatic cancer drug that experts predict will transform treatment for the notoriously deadly disease.
articles.body: The Food and Drug Administration on Wednesday approved a groundbreaking pancreatic cancer drug that experts predict will transform treatment for the notoriously deadly disease. The drug, Revolution Medicines’ Rasonque, or daraxonrasib, was approved for patients with advanced pancreatic cancer who have already tried a prior treatment, such as chemotherapy, the agency said. In a late-stage clinical trial of 500 patients, people who got the drug along with standard chemotherapy lived about twice as long — 13.2 months, on average — compared with people who got chemotherapy alone. Dr. Rachna Shroff, chief of the division of hematology and oncology at the University of Arizona Cancer Center in Tucson, previously told NBC News that she “started crying tears of joy” when she saw the trial’s preliminary findings in April. “It’s that big of a game changer for those of us who treat pancreatic cancer,” Shroff said. “It’s unprecedented.” The drug does have side effects, including a blistering rash, sores in the mouth and throat, and vomiting and diarrhea. (Former Sen. Ben Sasse of Nebraska, who got the drug in a clinical trial, described the rash as “nuclear” on a New York Times podcast in the spring.) Channing Der, a pharmacologist at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, called Wednesday’s approval a “monumental moment for the treatment of pancreatic cancer.” “Pancreatic cancer is the third leading cause of cancer death in the U.S. and the deadliest of all cancers,” Der wrote in an email. “This is just the beginning of more advances to come.” Taken as a daily pill, Rasonque targets a mutation in a gene called KRAS that’s found in nearly all pancreatic cancers as well as many lung, colorectal, ovarian and other cancers. The gene acts like an on/off switch controlling how cells grow in the body. The mutation causes it to get stuck in the “on” position, spurring cells to grow out of control. Scientists have known for years that if they could target the mutation, they could force the switch from its “on” position. But efforts have failed until Rasonque. “The is the start of the RAS revolution and it will be a sea change for cancer moving forward,” Shroff said Wednesday. More than 67,000 people in the U.S. are expected to be diagnosed with pancreatic cancer this year, according to the American Cancer Society. It’s one of the most difficult cancers to treat: There is no screening for the cancer, and early symptoms are often so vague that the majority of people are diagnosed at later stages of the disease, when it’s much more difficult to treat. The five-year survival rate for pancreatic adenocarcinoma — the most common form — is 8%. Revolution Medicines said that more than 2,000 patients have already received Rasonque under an expanded access program that the company started in May. The drugmaker said the out-of-pocket cost for Rasonque — before insurance and other discounts — will be $39,800 for a month’s supply.

articles.title: Dolly Parton’s private cancer battle highlights why some patients don’t share their diagnoses
articles.summary: Dolly Parton kept her cancer diagnosis private before her death, raising questions about why patients hide their battles and the stigma involved.
articles.body: Dolly Parton’s death on Tuesday followed a brief bout with cancer, according to statements from her family. "After bravely facing a brief battle with cancer, Dolly departed her Earthly life today at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center surrounded by loved ones," the family shared, as confirmed by Fox News Digital. The revelation of the singer’s previously undisclosed cancer battle raises questions about why some patients choose to keep a diagnosis private, even as public figures’ health struggles can spark wider awareness. DOLLY PARTON DEAD AT 80 Dr. Kristin Higgins, chief clinical officer at City of Hope Cancer Center in Atlanta, surmised that Parton may have preferred people remember her for her "amazing career" and not for a diagnosis at the end of her life. Keeping the disease private at first is a "very natural response," Higgins said, as a diagnosis can be very overwhelming. "It's very natural to cling to that identity of being a healthy, vibrant person without a diagnosis of cancer," she told Fox News Digital. "The patient really needs to acclimate to the idea of themselves having this disease and then start to tell friends and family kind of slowly after they go through that adjustment process." CANCER TREATMENT DELAYS SURGE ACROSS US AS DOCTOR WARNS SYSTEM ‘NEEDS FIXING IMMEDIATELY’ In some cases, Higgins said, people may withhold a cancer diagnosis due to some degree of shame or embarrassment. "Things like tobacco-related cancers, unfortunately, still carry a lot of stigma when diagnosed," she shared. "Patients may feel that it was their fault. And the reality is nobody deserves a cancer diagnosis." There are some benefits, however, to eventually sharing a cancer diagnosis with friends, family and community who can rally around the patient, according to the doctor. "For example, for people who are religious, letting their greater circle know about that diagnosis can be really helpful, as people will pray for them as they're going through the journey of treatment," Higgins said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "I think, overall, it's a very beneficial thing to eventually tell as many people as possible so you can get that support." The doctor also agreed that sharing a cancer journey can raise awareness and provide support to others facing the same challenge. "It's very natural to cling to that identity of being a healthy, vibrant person without a diagnosis of cancer." "If you are somebody with a cancer diagnosis, and you're beating it, and you are going through treatment successfully, other people seeing that — whether it's on social media or hearing it through a friend — that can be really helpful to an individual as they're facing a new cancer diagnosis," Higgins said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Another benefit of disclosing cancer is that it may open up more opportunities for treatment options. "There are so many resources out there now. … Clinical trials are really what moved the needle in the cure rates for cancer, and finding out about these trials is not easy," Higgins noted. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "So, the more people who know about your diagnosis, you have all these cheerleaders out there rooting for you, and you can get more information. You can hear more people's opinions about where you could seek the best cancer treatment." The doctor emphasized that there is more hope than ever for people facing a cancer diagnosis. "I think that's the beauty of sharing this diagnosis with the world is that we can get all the support we need."

articles.title: FDA approves once-daily pill for deadly cancer after patients' survival rates nearly double
articles.summary: Revolution Medicines' Rasonque targets the RAS protein driving 95% of pancreatic adenocarcinoma cases, offering a critical option after chemotherapy fails.
articles.body: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the use of a new cancer treatment pill Wednesday. Rasonque, manufactured by Revolution Medicines in California, is an inhibitor for the most common type of pancreatic cancer. The tablet, which is taken once daily, targets multiple forms of a protein called RAS that drives tumor growth. In a press release, the FDA called Rasonque a "new treatment option for patients with advanced pancreatic cancer," noting the agency approved it more than six months ahead of its review deadline. CANCER TREATMENT DELAYS SURGE ACROSS US AS DOCTOR WARNS SYSTEM ‘NEEDS FIXING IMMEDIATELY’ "Today’s approval provides a critical new option for patients facing an extraordinarily difficult and historically hard-to-treat cancer. It is our fundamental duty to deliver more cures and meaningful treatments to patients as quickly as possible," acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas said in a press release. "I am immensely proud of the dedicated FDA scientists whose fast, thorough review and relentless commitment made this groundbreaking milestone a reality." The authorization is for adults with metastatic pancreatic cancer that either did not respond to at least one prior treatment or could not receive certain combination drug therapies. Pancreatic adenocarcinoma remains one of the deadliest forms of oncology in the U.S., accounting for up to 95% of the roughly 67,000 annual pancreatic cancer cases identified by the National Cancer Institute. PATIENTS REMAIN CANCER-FREE NEARLY 3 YEARS AFTER RECEIVING EXPERIMENTAL IMMUNOTHERAPY While the disease makes up only 3.2% of total cancer diagnoses, it causes a disproportionately high number of cancer deaths because it is often found late and can spread quickly. The new drug was approved after a randomized, open-label trial of 500 patients with pre-treated metastatic disease. Patients taking Rasonque achieved a median overall survival of 13.2 months, nearly double the 6.7-month survival rate seen in the standard chemotherapy control group. "This drug showed unprecedented results in an area of high unmet need," said Angelo de Claro, M.D., director of the FDA’s Oncology Center of Excellence. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Regulators accelerated the medication's path to market by granting it priority review, orphan drug status and a breakthrough therapy designation. Additionally, the filing was evaluated using the FDA commissioner’s National Priority Voucher pilot program to speed up access to critical public health treatments. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Ahead of the official green light, the agency issued a "safe to proceed" letter in May, opening an expanded access protocol that allowed patients to receive the drug before final approval. Safety profiles show that the most frequent adverse events linked to Rasonque included rash, diarrhea, mouth sores (stomatitis), nausea, fatigue, vomiting, abdominal pain, fluid retention (edema), reduced appetite and bleeding (hemorrhage). TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "Today’s landmark approval is the most significant advance we have seen in the fight against pancreatic cancer, a devastating disease," said Anna Berkenblit, M.D., chief scientific and medical officer of the Pancreatic Cancer Action Network (PanCAN). CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I believe this drug will transform how pancreatic cancer is treated, giving people the opportunity for more time with loved ones, the possibility of a better quality of life and optimism that continued research may lead to even greater advances."

articles.title: Infant in Pennsylvania is one of two people reported to die of measles this week
articles.summary: The deaths were the first associated with measles in the state in 35 years.
articles.body: One of the two people who recently died of measles in Pennsylvania was an infant, the state Health Department said Wednesday. The department announced Tuesday that two unvaccinated residents had died of measles, the first measles-related deaths in the U.S. this year and the first in Pennsylvania in 35 years. On Wednesday, the department said one of those deaths was under investigation by the Lancaster County Coroner’s Office, which had said it was reviewing the death of an infant with a positive measles test. The Health Department did not specify the ages of either person who died. Both were residents of Lancaster County, where the share of kids who have gotten the MMR vaccine fell from 95.5% in 2017 to 87.6% last year. The Health Department has confirmed 424 measles cases this year, 94 of them diagnosed in the past week. So far, 73 people have been hospitalized for measles complications. The first dose of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine is recommended at 12 to 15 months and the second at 4 to 6 years. “The real vulnerability is in infants between 6 and 11 months of age, as maternal antibody is waning and they haven’t gotten their first dose of the MMR vaccine,” said Dr. Peter Hotez, dean of the National School of Tropical Medicine at Baylor College of Medicine in Dallas. In places where infants have a high risk of measles exposure, health authorities sometimes recommend an early dose of the vaccine for babies starting at 6 months old. That was the case during an outbreak in Texas last year, when two unvaccinated girls died of the disease. Nationwide, 2,777 measles cases have been confirmed this year, the most in 35 years. Measles has been considered eliminated in the U.S. since 2000 because it has not continuously spread over a yearlong period. The Pan American Health Organization is expected to decide in November whether the U.S. has lost its elimination status.
